第3根K线是在趋势线出现一次重要突破之后的一笔高1突破做多。第4根K线是一根空头反转K线，也是一个最终旗形做空的建仓形态——它出现在向上突破多头通道之后的那段买入高潮之后。另外，第3根K线那面旗形跌破了一条大的多头趋势线，说明空头正在积蓄一点点力量。只有在趋势线先被突破之后，才可以反向操作强趋势。而且，在强趋势里做逆势交易，需要一根 5 分钟（而不是 3 分钟或 1 分钟）的反转K线。当天剩下的盘后时段里，市场一直在一个窄幅交易区间里横盘。


> Bar 3 was a high 1 breakout long after a major trend line break. Bar 4 was a bear reversal bar and a setup for a final flag short following a buy climax after a breakout above a bull channel. Also, the bar 3 flag broke a big bull trend line, indicating that the bears were gaining a little strength. Fade a strong trend only if there was first a trend line break. Also, a countertrend trade in a strong trend needs a 5 minute (not a 3 or 1 minute) reversal bar. The market went sideways in a tight trading range for the rest of the postmarket session.


![图 14.2](figures/fig-14-02.jpg)


**图 14.2　盘前交易**


盘前是可以交易的，但在纽约证券交易所于太平洋标准时间上午 6:30 开盘之前的一两个小时里，通常没有太多入场点（见图 14.2）。不过，上午 5:30 常常会有报告公布，它们会带来快速的趋势和反转。


> The premarket is tradable, but there are usually not many entries in the hour or two before the New York Stock Exchange opens at 6:30 a.m. PST (see Figure 14.2). There are often reports at 5:30 a.m. that result in quick trends and reversals, though.


第1根K线是一笔楔形做多，也是一个双底，但交易者得一路持有、扛过第2根K线那次回调才能获利。楔形底部（也就是三次向下推进，或者这个形态许多其他叫法中的任何一种）通常会带来两段向上的行情。


> Bar 1 was a wedge long and a double bottom, but traders would have had to hold through the bar 2 pullback to make a profit. A wedge bottom (or three pushes down, or any of many other names for this pattern) usually leads to two legs up.


第2根K线是一个更高的低点，也是一次小型的趋势线反转。第3根K线是移动平均线处的高2。一份报告带来了一次向上的假突破，随后又出现了一根外包下跌K线（第4根K线）。交易者会在第3根K线下方做空，那里正是许多多头会挂止损单的位置。


> Bar 2 was a higher low and a small trend line reversal. Bar 3 was a high 2 at the moving average. A report resulted in a false breakout to the upside and then an outside down bar (bar 4). Traders would have shorted below bar 3, where many longs would have placed their stops.


第5根K线是一次突破回调。


> Bar 5 was a breakout pullback.


第6根K线是二次入场，它是从一个新的摆动低点向上反转的第二次尝试（第5根K线是第一次）。


> Bar 6 was a second entry for a second attempt to reverse up from a new swing low (bar 5 was the first).


![图 14.3](figures/fig-14-03.jpg)


**图 14.3　快市中最小报价单位图的K线更多**


如图 14.3 所示，Emini 小型合约对太平洋标准时间上午 5:30 公布的失业率报告反应很差。这是一张每根K线 100 个最小报价单位的图（即每根K线 100 笔成交），与每笔成交的量或时间都无关。注意，第1根到第5根K线之间的那 30 根K线，全都出现在一分钟之内，因为报告公布之后行情变动飞快。这些K线形成得太快，除了用市价单，用其它方式下单都会很困难，甚至根本来不及。从理论上说，根据价格行为可以做出许多次有利可图的剥头皮，但大多数交易者绝不该去尝试交易这种行情。展示这张图的唯一目的，是说明这些标准形态自始至终都存在。


> As shown in Figure 14.3, the Emini reacted poorly to the 5:30 a.m. PST unemployment report. This is a 100 tick chart where each bar represents 100 trades, independent of the volume of the trades or the time. Note that the 30 bars between bars 1 and 5 all occurred within one minute due to the fast action off the report. These bars were forming so rapidly that it would have been difficult or impossible to trade anything other than market orders. It was theoretically possible to make many profitable scalps based on the price action, but most traders should never attempt to trade this. The only purpose of showing it is to demonstrate that standard patterns were present throughout.


缩略图是同一段 30 分钟行情的 1 分钟图和 5 分钟图。


> The thumbnail charts are the 1 and 5 minute charts for the same 30 minutes of trading.


![图 14.4](figures/fig-14-04.jpg)


**图 14.4　Globex 电子盘与日盘常常有不同的建仓形态**


如图 14.4 所示，Globex 电子盘 24 小时时段的K线图上有一个扩张三角形，它结束于第5根K线的高点（第1根和第3根K线是头两次向上推进）；缩略图显示的是同一套编号下的日盘走势。做日盘交易的交易者并不需要看到 Globex 电子盘上这个扩张三角形，才在第5根K线处做空。第5根K线越过了昨天的高点，然后回调到移动平均线。市场随后反弹到一个更低的高点，并在第6根K线的双顶熊旗处出现了做空建仓形态（第一个顶出现在六根K线之前）。


> As shown in Figure 14.4, the bar chart of the Globex 24-hour session had an expanding triangle ending at the bar 5 high (bars 1 and 3 were the first two pushes up), and the thumbnail shows the day session with the same numbering. A day session trader did not need to see the Globex expanding triangle to go short at bar 5. Bar 5 took out yesterday's high and pulled back to the moving average. The market then bounced to a lower high and had a short setup at the bar 6 double top bear flag (the first top was six bars earlier).


# 第三部分　头一个小时（开盘区间）

*Part III　The First Hour (The Opening Range)*


我曾经和一位交易者在网上聊过很多次。他每次同时交易 100 份国债期货合约，但每天一到太平洋标准时间上午 7:30 至 8:00 就不见了。他说他研究过自己的交易结果，发现 85% 的利润都是在头一个小时里赚到的，于是他认定，自己在当天余下的时间里只是在情绪上把自己耗空，而这种消耗有时还会延续到第二天。因为这个缘故，他几年前就不再交易头一个小时之后的那段时间，光做头一个小时，而且做得非常好。


> I once had many online discussions with a trader who traded 100 Treasury bond futures contracts at a time, but he disappeared every day by 7:30 to 8:00 a.m. PST. He said that he studied his results and discovered that he made 85 percent of his profits in the first hour and decided that he just drained himself emotionally during the rest of the day, and sometimes this carried over into the next day. Because of this, he stopped trading after the first hour or so several years ago and was doing very well trading just the first hour.


以下是头一个小时的一些特征：


> Here are some of the characteristics of the first hour:


所谓头一个小时，其实很少真有一小时那么长。它指的是第一段像样的波段行情开始之前的那段时间，可能是 15 分钟，也可能是两个小时；人们常常把它叫做开盘区间。这是最容易赚钱的时段。有经验的剥头皮交易者都知道，反转很常见。这些人常常能做成许多精挑细选的剥头皮，因为他们押注突破尝试通常会失败——一天当中任何时候的突破尝试都是这样。他们要的是低买高卖。总的来说，他们会避开十字星信号K线，但常常在一次上涨之后做空多头或空头趋势K线的下方，或者在一次下跌之后做多多头或空头趋势K线的上方。同一个方向上连续的几根趋势K线，往往指示出他们下一次剥头皮的方向。连续两根强劲的多头趋势K线，通常会让剥头皮交易者想着做多；连续的几根空头趋势K线则会让他们偏向做空。这也是最容易亏钱的时段。新手看到大根的趋势K线，就怕错过一段巨大的突破。他们买得晚，买在强劲多头急速行情的顶部；做空也做得晚，空在强劲空头急速行情的底部，结果只是反复亏损。这个时段要考虑的变量更多，建仓形态来得也更快。由于他们常常把波段建仓形态和剥头皮建仓形态搞混，最后把交易管理得一塌糊涂。他们绝不该剥头皮，尤其是在头一个小时里。当K线很大时，交易者应该用更宽的止损，并把仓位规模调小。进入收盘时昨天留下的始终入场方向，往往会延续到今天开盘。反转很常见、很突然，而且幅度常常很大。如果你读价格行为的速度不够快，就等到市场慢下来、始终入场方向变得清楚为止。当天的第一根K线只有大约 20% 的概率会成为当天的高点或低点，所以不必觉得非要在第二根K线上入场。事实上，完全不必急着做任何一笔交易，因为用不了多久始终入场方向就会清楚，交易成功的概率也会更高。当天的高点或低点，通常总有一个会在头一个小时之内形成，所以波段交易者会耐心等待一个有可能成为当天极值之一的建仓形态。为当天高点或低点准备的建仓形态，往往只有 40% 的成功概率。既然回报可能比风险大很多倍，这笔波段交易的交易者等式仍可能非常出色。多数交易者应该把开盘区间里一次合乎逻辑的反转，当作当天最重要的那笔交易。这笔交易常常有五根或更多K线看起来都很糟，但随后会突然突破，在多数交易者眼里始终入场方向也就清楚了。在大多数交易日里，交易者都得做过不止一次反转，才能抓到一次成功的波段；但即使是那些走不远的尝试，通常也能小赚一点，或者只是小亏一点。对这类相对低概率的交易来说，这就构成了一个有利的交易者等式。当天的高点通常始于某种双顶，尽管它很少是精确的双顶。当天的低点通常始于某种不完美的双底。一旦始终入场方向变得清楚，交易者就可以用市价入场，也可以在任何一次小回调中入场做波段。有经验的剥头皮交易者会寻找回调，顺着趋势方向剥头皮。报告公布后的那几分钟里，交易由计算机程序主导；其中许多程序几乎在瞬间就拿到报告的数字版本，并用这些数据来生成交易。另一些程序依据统计规律交易，而不是基本面。在一个对手拥有「决策和下单都快得多」这一优势的环境里，要竞争是非常困难的。最好先等上一两根K线再入场。大多数交易日里都会出现跳空开盘（关于跳空开盘，见第 20 章）。开盘往往预告了这一天的类型。如果第一根K线是十字星，或者开头几根K线彼此重叠、并带着显眼的影线，那么这一天更可能出现大量双向交易。


> What is referred to as the first hour is rarely an hour. It is the time before the first good swing begins and can be 15 minutes or two hours; it is often called the opening range. It is the easiest time to make money. Experienced scalpers know that reversals are common. These traders can often make many carefully selected scalps, betting that breakout attempts will usually fail, as is typical of breakout attempts at any time of the day. They look to buy low and sell high. In general, they avoid doji signal bars, but will often short below either a bull or a bear trend bar after a move up, or buy above a bull or a bear trend bar after a move down. Consecutive trend bars in the same direction often indicate the direction of their next scalp. Two consecutive, strong bull trend bars will usually make scalpers look to buy, and consecutive bear trend bars will bias them in favor of shorts. It is the easiest time to lose money. Beginners see large trend bars and are afraid of missing a huge breakout. They buy late, at the top of strong bull spikes, and short late, at the bottom of strong bear spikes, only to take repeated losses. There are more variables to consider, and the setups come faster. Because they often confuse swing and scalp setups, they end up managing their trades wrong. They should never scalp, especially in the first hour. When the bars are big, traders should use wider stops and trade smaller size. Yesterday's always-in direction going into the close often carries over into the open of today. Reversals are common, abrupt, and often large. If you can't read the price action fast enough, wait until the market slows down and the always-in direction becomes clear. The first bar of the day is the high or low of the day only about 20 percent of the time, so don't feel a need to enter on the second bar. In fact, there is no need to rush to take any trade, because before long the always-in direction will be clear, and the probability of a successful trade will be higher. Either the high or low of the day usually forms within the first hour, so swing traders patiently wait for a setup that can be one of the extremes of the day. The setup for the high or low of the day often has only a 40 percent probability of success. Since the reward can be many times larger than the risk, the trader's equation can still be excellent for a swing trade. Most traders should focus on a logical reversal in the opening range for their most important trade of the day. The trade often looks bad for five or more bars, but then suddenly breaks out and the always-in direction becomes clear to most traders. On most days, a trader will have to take more than one reversal before catching a successful swing, but even the ones that don't go far usually make a small profit or have only a small loss. This creates a favorable trader's equation for this particular type of relatively low-probability trade. The high of the day usually begins with some type of double top, although it is rarely exact. The low of the day usually begins with an imperfect double bottom of some type. Once the always-in direction becomes clear, traders can enter at the market or on any small pullback for a swing. Experienced scalpers look for pullbacks to scalp in the direction of the trend. Trading in the minutes after a report is dominated by computer programs, many of which get a nearly instantaneous numerical version of the report and use the data to generate trades. Other programs trade off statistics and not fundamentals. It is very difficult to compete in an environment where your opponent has the edge of being much faster at making decisions and placing trades. It is better to wait for a bar or two before entering. Gap openings are present on most days (see Chapter 20 on gap openings). The open often foretells the type of day. If the first bar is a doji or the first several bars overlap and have prominent tails, the day is more likely to have lots of two-sided trading.


太平洋标准时间上午 7:00 常常有报告发布。即使某个报告并没有在网上列出，市场通常也会表现得像是有报告一样。计算机在分析速度和下单速度上拥有明显优势，而它们就是你的竞争对手。当你的竞争对手拥有巨大优势时，不要去和它竞争。等它们的优势消失，等到速度不再重要时再去交易。


> There are often reports at 7:00 a.m. PST. Even if a report is not listed on the Internet, the market usually behaves as if there was a report. Computers have a clear edge in speed of analysis and order placement, and they are your competitors. When your competition has a big advantage, don't compete. Wait for their edge to disappear and trade when speed is no longer important.


头一个小时——更准确地说，开盘区间——是市场为当天第一段趋势做准备的时段，一旦那段趋势开始，这个时段就结束了。它常常持续一两个小时，有时短到只有 15 分钟。这是最容易赚钱的时段，也是最容易亏钱的时段。原因是许多交易者没法足够快地处理所有变量，而且信息有限，因为当天还没有多少根K线。他们必须决定一笔交易是当波段做、当剥头皮做，还是两者都做；还必须依据交易者等式里的三个变量——概率、风险、回报——来做这个决定；而他们所处的环境通常是：有经济报告要发布，反转以及随之而来的决策频繁出现，K线又常常大得不寻常，因此他们必须把风险调整到远高于平常的水平——这和一天中的其他时段不同，那些时段里风险通常固定在一个特定大小上，一般不需要多想。明白了吧？交易者要考虑的更多，用来思考的时间却更少。计算机在分析速度和下单速度上拥有明显优势，而它们就是你的竞争对手。当你的竞争对手拥有巨大优势时，不要去和它竞争。如果你心里想的是「天啊，我真希望自己也有那些用计算机做程序化交易的公司所拥有的速度优势」，那你就该明白自己处于劣势。等它们的优势消失，等到速度不再重要时再去交易。


> The first hour or, more accurately, the opening range is the time when the market is setting up the first trend of the day, and it ends once that trend begins. It often lasts for a couple of hours and sometimes is as short as 15 minutes. It is the easiest time to make money, but is the easiest time to lose money as well. This is because many traders cannot process all of the variables fast enough, and the information is limited, since there are not many bars yet in the day. They have to decide on whether to treat a trade as a swing, a scalp, or both, and have to base the decision on the three trader's equation variables of probability, risk, and reward, in an environment when there are usually economic reports, where reversals and therefore decisions come often, and where the bars are often unusually large and therefore require them to adjust their risk to much larger than normal, as opposed to other times during the day when risk is a variable that is usually fixed at a certain size and does not usually require much thought. Get the picture? A trader has more to think about and less time to do the thinking. Computers have a clear edge in speed of analysis and order placement, and they are your competitors. When your competition has a big advantage, don't compete. If you are thinking, “Boy, I wish that I had the speed advantage that the firms using computers for program trading have,” then you realize that you are at a disadvantage. Wait for their edge to disappear and trade when speed is no longer important.


交易本来就够难了，优势永远都很小，而头一个小时额外增加的复杂度，可能把交易者推到超出其有效交易能力的境地。如果要考虑的变量太多、以至于没法盈利地交易，交易者可以通过减少变量来提高成功的机会。比如，他们可以决定只找高概率的剥头皮，或者只找可能性大的波段建仓形态；也可以等到出现明确的始终入场交易，然后做波段，或者顺着那个方向剥头皮，在回调中入场。他们还可以把仓位做成平常的一半到四分之一，并使用放在信号K线之外的保护性止损——这往往要求止损比平时大两倍甚至更多。


> Trading is difficult enough and the edge is always small, and the added complexity of the first hour can push traders beyond their ability to trade effectively. If there are too many variables to consider to trade profitably, traders can increase their chances of success by reducing the number of variables. For example, they can decide to look only for high-probability scalps or for only likely swing setups, or they can wait until there is a clear always-in trade and then swing, or take scalps in that direction, entering on pullbacks. They can also trade half to a quarter of their normal size and use a protective stop that is beyond the signal bar, which often requires a stop that is two or more times larger than their usual size.


造成亏损的最大原因之一，是交易者分不清波段建仓形态和剥头皮建仓形态。从交易者等式出发，读者已经知道，剥头皮交易者一般必须做到 60% 或更高的胜率，因为风险通常必须与回报差不多大。剥头皮建仓形态比波段建仓形态常见得多，但大多数剥头皮建仓形态并没有 60% 的成功概率，应该避开。不过，头一个小时里反转很常见，交易者往往没有足够的时间去充分评估交易者等式。如果他们的默认做法是每一笔反转都做、做完之后再算账，长期下来就会亏钱。当天的高点或低点，往往跟在一个成功概率不到 50% 的建仓形态后面；对剥头皮来说这是个糟糕的建仓形态，但对波段来说它仍然可能是极好的建仓形态。


> One of the biggest causes of losses is a trader's inability to distinguish between swing and scalp setups. From the trader's equation, readers know that scalpers generally have to win on 60 percent or more of their trades, since the risk usually has to be about the size of the reward. Scalp setups are much more common than swing setups, but most scalp setups do not have a 60 percent probability of success and should be avoided. However, reversals are common in the first hour, and traders often do not have enough time to adequately assess the trader's equation. If their default is to take every reversal and then do the math after they are in, they will lose over time. The high or low of the day often follows a setup that has less than a 50 percent chance of success, and is therefore a terrible setup for a scalp, but it can still be a great setup for a swing.


有经验的交易者通常能在头一个小时里找到四笔或更多剥头皮，甚至靠这些交易谋生。举例来说，如果他们平均每天做成两笔各两个点的盈利剥头皮，并且交易 25 份 Emini 小型合约，那么一年就能赚到一百万美元。多数交易者在必须在很短时间内、并且手上只有五根或 10 根K线信息的情况下，都无法可靠地评估风险、回报和概率，所以在头一个小时里、在反转来得又快又突然的时候，他们不该做剥头皮。相反，他们应该耐心等待一个可能引出始终入场波段行情的建仓形态，或者等到波段已经开始、市场有了清楚的始终入场方向，再去做一笔波段。这样他们的回报就会大于风险（可能是风险的两倍或三倍）；而且既然始终入场方向很清楚，市场朝他们的方向至少走出与他们止损处风险相同数量的最小报价单位的机会就有 60% 或更好，到那时他们就可以把止损移到保本。


> Experienced traders can usually find four or more scalps in the first hour and even make a living off those trades. For example, if they average two profitable scalps a day of two points each and trade 25 Emini contracts, they could make a million dollars a year. Since most traders cannot process the risk, reward, and probability reliably when they have to do it quickly and with only five or 10 bars of information, they should not scalp in the first hour when reversals come quickly and abruptly. Instead, they should wait patiently for a setup that is likely to lead to an always-in swing, or wait until the swing has begun and the market has a clear always-in direction, and then take a swing trade. They will then have a reward that is larger than their risk (it may be two or three times as large), and since the always-in direction is clear, they'll have a 60 percent or better chance of the market going at least as many ticks in their direction as they have at risk from their stop, at which point they can move their stop to breakeven.


许多有经验的交易者会在头一个小时里寻找一根强劲趋势K线或连续几根趋势K线，然后对一次回调做剥头皮。举例来说，如果先出现连续两根强劲的多头趋势K线，接着出现一根十字星K线，他们可能会在十字星K线低点及其下方挂限价买单。由于他们把这看成偏弱的反转信号，尤其是在如此强劲的多头急速行情之后，他们预期它会失败。这意味着在K线下方卖出过的空头必须买回自己的空单，而且很可能至少有一两根K线不想再卖。这把空头清出了市场，还把一部分空头变成了买家，于是做多的剥头皮交易者就有了赚钱的好机会。保护性止损的大小和止盈目标的大小，取决于K线有多大。如果 Emini 的日均波动幅度约为 15 个点，而多头趋势K线大约有两个点那么高，那么交易者可能冒着大约两个点的风险去赚两个点——前提是他们相信成功概率有 60%，而在这类情况下往往确实如此。另一些多头可能会在更低处分批建仓，把风险放在多头急速行情底部之下。只有非常有经验的交易者才应该在头一个小时里反向操作K线的突破，因为行情可能速度很快、走得很远，交易者必须对自己的判读、以及在快速波动的市场里管理交易的能力有非常大的信心。


> Many experienced traders look for a strong trend bar or consecutive trend bars in the first hour, and then will scalp a pullback. For example, if there are two consecutive strong bull trend bars and then a doji bar, they might place limit orders to buy at or below the low of the doji bar. Since they see it as a weak reversal signal, especially after such a strong bull spike, they expect it to fail. This means that the bears who sold below the bar will have to buy back their shorts and probably won't want to sell again for at least a bar or two. This removes bears from the market and turns some bears into buyers, which gives the bull scalpers a good chance to make a profit. The protective stop size and target size depend on how large the bars are. If the Emini has had an average daily range of about 15 points and the bull trend bars are about two points tall, traders might risk about two points to make two points, if they believe that there is a 60 percent chance of success, which there often is in these circumstances. Other bulls might scale in lower and risk to below the bottom of the bull spike. Only very experienced traders should be fading breakouts of bars in the first hour, because the moves can be fast and go very far, and traders have to be very confident of their read and their ability to manage their trades in a fast, volatile market.


头一个小时里的行情可能很快，交易者常常被大根趋势K线带来的兴奋冲昏头，入场太晚。他们知道趋势很快就要开始，怕错过，结果反而被一次反转套住。由于市场在头一个小时里一直在寻找方向，反转很常见。交易者可能做了一笔交易，以为自己会拿成波段，结果发现它下一根K线就反转了。接着他们必须决定，是出场，还是依靠放在信号K线之外的止损。几乎每次都是这样：就在做这个决定的时候，他们意识到那笔反转交易比自己做的这笔更好，于是又纠结于怎么把亏损压到最小、同时换到反方向的那笔交易里去。他们等得太久，盼着一次回调，最后出场时的亏损比自己原打算承受的更大。不仅如此，大亏让他们心烦意乱，在下一笔交易之前还得先缓过来。等他们准备好再交易时，市场已经朝着新方向走得太远，他们不敢再进场，尽管那段趋势看着很强。一天结束时，他们把图打印出来，简直不敢相信那些建仓形态当时竟然那么清楚。但事后回看和实时盘面是完全不同的两回事。


> The moves in the first hour can be fast, and traders often get caught up in the excitement of big trend bars and enter late. They know that a trend will soon begin and are fearful of missing it, and instead get caught in a reversal. Since the market is searching for direction in the first hour, reversals are common. Traders might take a trade and think that they will swing it, only to discover that it reverses on the next bar. They then have to decide whether to exit or to rely on a stop beyond the signal bar. Invariably, as they are making that decision, they realize that the reversal trade is better than the trade they took, and they struggle with trying to figure out how to minimize their loss and get into a trade in the other direction. They hold too long, hoping for a pullback, and then exit with a larger loss than they planned on taking. Not only that; they are upset by the large loss and need to recover before taking the next trade. Once they are ready to trade again, the market has moved so far in the new direction that they are afraid to take the trade, even though the trend looks strong. At the end of the day, they print the chart out and cannot believe how clear the setups actually were. But hindsight is very different from real time.


交易者也可能在那些本该做成波段的剥头皮上亏钱。如果他们本周早些时候在几笔自以为是好波段的交易上亏了钱，今天开盘时他们就会对做波段心存警惕。假设本周有几次，市场已经走得足够远、够剥头皮交易者赚一笔，但随后很快反转，把他们止损出局、造成亏损。于是今天他们决定，头一个小时里的每一笔交易都只做剥头皮。前两笔剥头皮就亏了；而在第二笔被止损出局时，那根触发止损的K线反转成了一根外包K线，并引出一段非常强劲的趋势，方向正是他们已经不再持有的那笔交易。由于他们决定只做反转上的剥头皮，市场一根K线接一根K线地不断走出趋势时，他们只能在场外看着。这段趋势走了八个点才出现一次回调，他们这才突然意识到，这一笔波段交易提供的利润，抵得上四次成功的剥头皮。


> Traders can also lose money on scalps that should be swings. If they lost several times earlier in the week on what they thought were good swing trades, they will be wary of swing trading on the open today. Assume that several times this week the market went far enough for a scalper's profit, but quickly reversed and stopped them out with a loss. Today, they decide to scalp every trade in the first hour. They lose on the first two scalps, but when they were stopped out on the second trade, the bar that hit the stop reversed into an outside bar and led to a very strong trend in the direction of the trade that they no longer held. Since they decided that they wanted to trade only scalps on reversals, they are on the sidelines as the market trends relentlessly, bar after bar. The trend runs for eight points before there is a pullback, and they suddenly realize that this one swing trade offered as much profit as four successful scalps.


当他们因为做了低概率的建仓形态、做剥头皮接连亏了好几天；又因为频繁被止损而放弃尝试波段（结果一放弃就错过一大段趋势），他们会既困惑又沮丧。他们觉得自己什么都做对了却还是在亏，觉得交易太不公平：「为什么别人在头一个小时里能做得那么好，而我怎么做都亏？」原因在于他们想做的太多了。他们在正在成形的交易区间顶部买入、底部卖出，指望突破成功，不承认多数突破尝试都会失败这个现实。接着，他们又不肯做最好的那个波段建仓形态，因为它看起来弱、看起来多半会失败——就像过去一小时里前五次反转那样。当交易者有这种感觉时，他们应该先停下开盘区间的交易，直到始终入场方向变得清楚。没错，这样一来他们要等趋势已经走了两三个点之后才入场，能赚的也更少，但成功的可能性大得多。宁可每次赚一点、但经常赚，也远好过一天亏上好几笔、还指望着最终能搞明白怎么靠头一个小时盈利。


> After several days of losing when they tried to scalp because they took low-probability setups, and having given up on trying to swing because they got stopped out so often (only to miss a big trend after they gave up), they are confused and upset. They feel like they did everything right but still lost, and that trading is so unfair: “Why can other people do so well in the first hour, yet I lose no matter what I do?” It is because they are trying to do too much. They are buying at the top and selling at the bottom of the developing range, hoping for a successful breakout, denying the reality that most breakout attempts fail. They then do not take the best swing setup, because it looks weak and it looks like it will probably fail, just like the past five reversals in the past hour. When traders feel this way, they should take a break from trading the opening range until the always-in position is clear. Yes, they will be entering after the trend has already gone a couple of points and they stand to make less, but the chance of success is much greater. It is far better to win a little, but win frequently, than it is to lose several times a day while hoping to finally figure out how to trade the first hour profitably.


能成功做剥头皮的交易者，往往不得不在头一个小时里做出调整。一般来说，剥头皮交易者通常必须冒与回报差不多大的风险，但既然最好的做法永远是先看清需要多少风险，他们可以在确定风险之后再定一个合理的回报目标。比如，如果 Emini 里的K线通常大约两个点高，而今天大约有四个点高，交易者可能就得冒大约四个点的风险。市场走得很快，一边要读图、一边要下单，很难再花时间做精确计算。剥头皮交易者应该干脆快速地把仓位规模减半，或者砍掉三分之二。具体怎么做并不重要，重要的是做得快、不再去想它，把精力放在更重要的事上：正确判读和下单。如果在必要的时候不愿意用更大的止损，那就不该做这笔交易。另外，一旦交易者已经入场，市场回撤得比他们认为应该有的幅度更深（但没打到他们的止损），随后行情重新启动、却看起来比他们认为应该有的更弱，这时他们必须愿意在更小的止盈目标处出场。比如，大根K线可能迫使他们在 Emini 交易上冒四个点而不是两个点的风险，但一旦行情朝他们那边走起来，看起来却偏弱。如果他们相信自己的前提已经不再成立，就必须能够改变目标；这时只赚一两个点就出场、然后再等更多信息，往往是值得的。


> Traders who can scalp successfully often have to make adjustments in the first hour. In general, scalpers usually have to risk about as much as their reward, but since it is always best to begin by looking at what risk is required, they can set a reasonable reward after determining their risk. For example, if the bars in the Emini are usually about two points tall, but they are about four points tall today, a trader might have to risk about four points. The market is moving quickly and it is difficult to spend time doing exact math while trying to read the charts and to place orders. Scalpers should just quickly cut the position size in half or by two-thirds. It doesn't matter what they do. What matters is that they do it quickly, stop thinking about it, and concentrate on what is much more important: reading correctly and placing orders. If they are unwilling to use a larger stop when it is necessary, they should not take the trade. Also, once traders are in the trade and the market pulls back further than they think it should have (but does not hit their stop), and then the move resumes but looks weaker than they think it should, they have to be willing to get out at a smaller profit target. For example, the large bars might force them to risk four points instead of two on an Emini trade, but once the move has gone their way, it looks weak. If they believe that their premise is no longer valid, they have to be able to change their goal, and it is often worth exiting with just a point or two profit and then waiting for more information.


只有那种能迅速应对仓位、止损和止盈目标大小变化的交易者，才应该尝试这么做。因为剥头皮通常要求风险与回报一样大，也就要求很高的胜率，所以多数交易者应该避开剥头皮，尤其是在头一个小时里。如果多数交易者能等到市场明确处于始终入场状态，然后再做一笔波段，他们长期盈利的机会就更大。这意味着等距运动出现的概率有 60% 或更高。这样他们就可以使用一个至少和风险一样大、最好是风险两倍大的止盈目标，从而拥有一个有利的交易者等式。


> Only experienced traders, who can handle changing position, stop, and profit target sizes quickly, should attempt it. Because scalping usually requires a risk that is as large as the reward, and therefore a high winning percentage, most traders should avoid scalps, especially in the first hour. Most traders have a better chance of being profitable in the long run if they can wait for a clearly always-in market and then take a swing trade. This means that the probability of an equidistant move is 60 percent or more. They can then use a profit target that is at least as large as the risk, and preferably twice the size of the risk, and have a favorable trader's equation.


由于头一个小时里反转很多，在市场明确变成始终做多或始终做空之前，最好还是着眼于低买高卖。遗憾的是，许多交易者做的恰恰相反。他们看到大根的多头或空头趋势K线，就担心自己错过了突破——而这种突破几乎总是失败。他们必须学会等待一个得到确认的突破和明确的始终入场市场。到那时，他们才该转而采用波段的做法：市场始终做多时，愿意在靠近顶部的位置买入；市场始终做空时，愿意在靠近底部的位置卖出。如果交易者无法迅速区分波段建仓形态和剥头皮建仓形态，就不该仓促做决定。相反，他们应该耐心等待一个清楚的始终入场信号，然后再开始交易。多数交易者没法在头一个小时里成功剥头皮，更不可能先剥头皮、再在时机成熟时切换到波段交易。他们应该做的，是耐心等待波段建仓形态。


> Because the first hour has many reversals, it is better to look to buy low and sell high until the market becomes clearly always-in long or short. Unfortunately, many traders do the opposite. They see large trend bars up or down and are afraid that they are missing a breakout, which almost always fails. They have to learn to wait for a confirmed breakout and a clear always-in market. Then they should switch to a swing approach and become willing to buy near the top when the market is always-in long, or sell near the bottom when it is always-in short. If traders cannot quickly distinguish swing setups from scalp setups, they should not make rash decisions. Instead, they should wait patiently for a clear always-in signal and then begin trading. Most traders cannot successfully scalp in the first hour, and certainly are unable to scalp initially and then switch to swing trading when the time is right. They should instead wait patiently for swing setups.


既然头一两个小时经常提供能带来极好波段交易的建仓形态，交易者就必须做好准备去抓它们。虽然人们倾向于认为头一个小时里的形态有所不同，但事实上，从价格行为的角度看，它们并没有不同。建仓形态和一天中任何其他时段、任何时间级别上的建仓形态都一样。不同的是，波动性往往更大，因此形态走得更远，而且反转常常突然得出人意料。反转看起来偏弱、在趋势突破之前先出现两三根虚弱的十字星K线，这很常见。要明白这很常见；如果你已经入场又看到这种疲弱，不要急着打平出场。相信自己的判读，因为你很可能判对了，而且你有可能赚到一笔丰厚的波段利润。


> Since the first hour or two frequently provides setups that result in great swing trades, traders must be ready to take them. Although there is a tendency to think that the patterns are different in the first hour, the reality is that from a price action perspective, they are not. The setups are the same as during any other time of the day and on any time frame. What is different is that the volatility is often greater and therefore the patterns run further, and the reversals are often unexpectedly abrupt. It is common for reversals to look weak and have two or three weak doji bars before the trend breaks out. Realize that this is common and, if you entered and see this weakness, don't scratch out. Rely on your read because you will likely be right, and you stand to make a large swing profit.


开盘还有一个不同之处：许多交易的建仓形态是基于昨天的价格行为形成的。昨天最后几个小时里常常会走出一段通道，随后今天开盘时会突破它，或者出现一个远在那面旗形之外的市场跳空。无论哪种情况，都要留意反转和延续。记住，通道就是旗形，所以多头通道就是熊旗，空头通道就是牛旗。另外，如果昨天收盘时市场明确处于始终做多或始终做空状态，交易者应该假定这波趋势会在今天开盘后延续下去，直到看见相反的证据为止。


> One other difference about the open is that many trades set up based on yesterday's price action. There will often be a channel that develops in the final couple of hours of yesterday followed by either a breakout or a market gap well beyond that flag on today's open. In either case, watch for reversals and continuations. Remember, a channel is just a flag, so a bull channel is a bear flag and a bear channel is a bull flag. Also, if the market ended clearly always-in long or short, traders should assume that the trend will continue on the open until they see evidence to the contrary.


最后一个重要区别是：在大多数交易日里，当天的高点或低点出现在头一个小时左右；对于那些有可能成为当天高点或低点的交易，试着把其中一部分拿成波段是有好处的。如果你持有的交易有这种潜力，而市场又朝着你的方向强劲运行，就用保本止损，让自己有机会收下开盘后经常出现的那笔意外之财般的利润。


> A final important difference is that the high or low of the day occurs in the first hour or so on most days, and it is beneficial to try to swing part of any trade that might be the high or low of the day. If you are in a trade with such potential and the market moves strongly in your direction, use a breakeven stop to allow yourself to collect the windfall profits that often happen off the open.


虽然头一个小时左右出现的任何一次反转都有可能造出当天的高点或低点，但某一次具体反转做到这一点的概率通常不超过 50%。如果交易者改为等待反转之后出现清楚的后续行情和明确的始终入场走势，那么这次反转成为当天高点或低点的概率常常超过 60%。等待始终入场确认的交易者为这个更高的概率付出的代价是更小的利润，而偏好只做高概率交易的交易者对这种取舍很满意。由于为当天高点或低点准备的建仓形态往往只有 40% 到 50% 的确定性，它通常是个很糟的剥头皮建仓形态，尽管它对波段交易来说有着很强的交易者等式。趋势在开始的时候往往走得很慢，看上去完全不像趋势，但通常在五根K线左右之内就会突破，进入明确的始终入场市场。大多数情况下，多头趋势日的建仓形态是某种双底的一部分，尽管它通常不完美到根本看不出是双底。同样，空头趋势日的建仓形态通常是不完美双顶的一部分。举例来说，如果开盘后出现一连串强劲的多头趋势K线，然后出现一次不完全的回调，并在五到 10 根K线之后被回测，这就形成了一个双底牛旗建仓形态，很有可能引出当天的新高。随后的突破可能走出一段向上的等距运动，并引出一段多头趋势。


> Although any reversal in the first hour or so can create the high or low of the day, the probability of any one particular reversal doing so is usually not more than 50 percent. If a trader instead waits for clear follow-through and a clear always-in move after the reversal, the probability that the reversal will be the high or low of the day is often more than 60 percent. The traders who wait for the always-in confirmation pay for that increased probability with smaller profits, but traders who prefer to take only high-probability trades are happy with the trade-off. Since the high or low of the day setup is often only 40 to 50 percent certain, it is usually a bad scalp setup, even though it has a strong trader's equation for a swing trade. The trend, as it begins, often starts slowly and does not look like a trend at all, but usually within five bars or so has a breakout into a clear always-in market. Most of the time, the setup for a bull trend day is part of a double bottom of some type, even though it is usually so imperfect that it does not look like a double bottom. Likewise, the setup for a bear trend day is usually part of an imperfect double top. For example, if there is a series of strong bull trend bars off the open and then a partial pullback that gets tested five to 10 bars later, this forms a double bottom flag entry and has a good chance of leading to a new high of the day. The breakout then might run for a measured move up and lead to a bull trend.


交易者常常在当天第二根K线突破第一根K线的高点或低点时入场，但视情况而定，成功剥头皮的概率往往不到 50%。这意味着交易者等式只对波段成立；可交易者常常错误地把这笔交易当成剥头皮来做，而在概率约为 50%、风险又与回报一样大的时候，这么做就是亏钱的路子。他们说服自己会拿成波段、会扛过回调，但往往一两根K线之内就抓个小利跑了，还觉得松了口气。他们其实本想剥头皮，只是自己没意识到；到了月底他们会纳闷自己怎么会亏钱，原因就是他们做了一笔交易者等式为负的交易。头一个小时里的有些反转，有 70% 的概率能达到剥头皮的目标，却只有 40% 的概率达到波段目标。交易者必须在进场之前就知道自己打算怎么管理这笔交易，因为进场之后改变目标是亏钱的策略。你不能带着一个前提进场，却按另一个前提来管理交易；但在头一个小时里，一切都发生得那么快，K线又大，在形成过程中K线内部还有大幅回撤，交易者把剥头皮和波段搞混是很常见的。


> Traders often enter on the second bar of the day as it breaks beyond the high or low of the first bar, but the probability of a successful scalp is often under 50 percent, depending on the situation. That means that the trader's equation makes sense only for a swing, but traders often mistakenly treat the trade like a scalp, which is a losing approach when the probability is about 50 percent and the risk is as large as the reward. They convince themselves that they will swing and hold through pullbacks, but within a bar or two, they grab a small profit and feel relieved. They really intended to scalp but did not realize it, and they will wonder at the end of the month why they lost money. It is because they took a trade that had a losing trader's equation. Some reversals in the first hour have a 70 percent chance of reaching a scalper's target, but only a 40 percent chance of reaching a swing target. Traders have to know in advance how they plan to manage the trade before they take it, because changing goals after entering is a losing strategy. You can't have one premise and then manage the trade as if it was based on a different premise, but it is common for traders to confuse scalps and swings in the first hour when everything happens so quickly and the bars are large and have big pullbacks within the bars as they are forming.


当天第一根K线成为当天高点或低点的概率约为 20%（有大幅跳空开盘的日子除外，如果这根K线是一根强劲趋势K线，概率可以达到 50% 或更高）。另外，这根K线往往很大，常常相当于一个平常交易日最终波动幅度的 20% 左右。举例来说，如果 Emini 的平均波动幅度约为 10 个点，而今天第一根K线两个点高，那么当第二根K线突破第一根K线时买入的交易者，赚到八个点的概率约为 20%，而承担的风险是两个点略多一点。这就是一个亏钱的交易者等式。如果交易者非常擅长主观地评估所有变量、并挑选出概率更高的交易，他们可以拥有数学上的优势；但基于当天第一根K线的这类高概率交易，大约一个月才出现一次。即使交易者在回报达到风险两倍时就止盈，他们一个月也只能成功一两次，所以在当天第二根K线上寻找波段入场很少值得去做。不过，既然在大多数交易日里，头一个小时里都会出现一次可靠的波段机会——回报是风险的两倍——那么如果开盘不久就出现一个强势反转建仓形态，交易者就该考虑把这笔交易拿成波段。一旦趋势走到大约止损的两倍大，他们就可以把止损移到保本，并把交易的一部分拿成波段，直到出现始终入场方向的反转。


> The first bar of the day has about a 20 percent chance of being either the high or low of the day (except on days where there is a large gap opening, when the probability can be 50 percent or more if the bar is a strong trend bar). Also, the bar is often large, frequently about 20 percent of an average day's ultimate range. For example, if the average range in the Emini has been about 10 points and the first bar of today is two points tall, a trader who buys as the second bar breaks above the first bar has about a 20 percent chance of making eight points while risking a little more than two points. This is a losing trader's equation. If traders are very good at subjectively evaluating all of the variables and selecting trades with a higher probability, they can have a mathematical edge, but these high-probability trades based on the first bar of the day happen only about once a month. Even if traders take profits once the reward is twice the size of the risk, they will be successful only a couple of times a month, so looking for a swing entry on the second bar of the day is rarely worthwhile. However, since a reliable swing in the first hour, where the reward is twice the size of the risk, occurs on most days, if there is a strong reversal setup early on, traders should consider swinging the trade. Once the trend reaches about twice the size of their stop, they can move their stop to breakeven and swing part of the trade until there is an always-in reversal.


有时市场在当天的第一两根K线上就走出趋势，而第一根K线最终成为当天的一个极值。当市场一开盘就走出趋势时，及早入场很重要，但不一定非要在第二根K线入场。这种形态在跳空开盘时最常见，无论跳空大小。当你入场时可能是站在一段巨大趋势的起点上，这时尤其重要的是试着把一部分合约拿成波段。如果形态非常强，你可以把大部分合约都拿成波段，然后迅速把止损移到保本。


> Sometimes the market trends for the first bar or two of the day and that first bar ends up as one of the extremes of the day. When the market trends from the open, it is important to enter early, but not necessarily on the second bar. This pattern is most common with gap openings, large or small. When you enter a trade where you might be at the start of a huge trend, it is particularly important to try to swing some contracts. If the pattern is very strong, you could swing most of your contracts and then quickly move your stop to breakeven.


不过，如果强势开盘被反转（也就是朝反方向突破、创出当天新极值），那么这一天可能转为反方向的趋势，也可能变成交易区间日。开盘后的强势趋势即使被反转，也仍然说明有交易者愿意朝那个方向激进交易；如果这次反转势头减弱，他们当天晚些时候会很快再次朝那个方向交易。


> However, if the strong opening is reversed (a breakout to a new extreme of the day in the opposite direction), then the day might trend in the opposite direction or it could turn into a trading range day. A strong trend off the open, even if it is reversed, still means that there were traders willing to trade aggressively in that direction, and they will be quick to trade again in that direction later in the day if the reversal falters.


如果你认为一次向下反转并不是当天的高点，你的把握也绝不该超过 30%；因为那样一来，你就至少有 70% 的把握认为它不是高点，而在开盘区间正在形成的时候，市场从来没有那么确定过。〔译注：原文此处的因果表述前后不一致，作者的本意是：任何单次反转是否就是当日高点的判断，把握都不该超过三成。〕事实上，在一天里的任何时候，很少有事情能有那么确定。那种优势实在太大了，还没等它确定到那个程度，交易者早就把它抹平了。不要对某个看法太执着，尤其是在头一个小时里，因为即使是最强的行情，也可能在下一根K线上急剧反转。不过，虽然头一两个小时里的反转只有 30% 到 40% 的概率会成为当天的高点或低点，但如果后续行情良好，这个可能性可以很快升到 50% 到 60%。


> If you think that a reversal down is not the high of the day, you should never be more than 30 percent certain, because you would then be at least 70 percent certain that it is not, and the market is never that certain when the opening range is forming. In fact, rarely is anything that certain at any time of the day. That edge is simply too large, and traders would quickly neutralize it long before it got that certain. Don't get too committed to an opinion, especially in the first hour, because even the strongest moves can reverse sharply on the next bar. However, although a reversal in the first couple of hours might have only a 30 to 40 percent chance of becoming the high or low of the day, if there is good follow-through, the odds can quickly increase to 50 to 60 percent.


尽管大多数开盘后的反转只适合剥头皮、不适合波段，但当某一次反转特别强时，交易者应该试着把至少一半的仓位拿成波段。前面已经提到，头一两个小时往往是一天里最有可能找到「能赚到风险两到三倍」这类交易的时段。总的来说，多数交易者应该下足功夫去抓头一两个小时里那些有潜力的波段交易，因为这类交易在回报、风险和概率上的交易者等式组合是最好的。


> Even though most early reversals are good for scalps and not swings, when one is particularly strong, a trader should try to swing at least half of the position. As mentioned earlier, there is a tendency for the first hour or two to be the most likely time of the day to find a trade where a trader can make two to three times the risk. In general, most traders should work very hard to take potential swing trades in the first hour or two because those trades have the best trader's equation combination of reward, risk, and probability.


为什么市场会在开头几根K线里走出一段大行情，然后反转？为什么它不是干脆就开在当天的低点或高点？当天开盘价的位置不是由哪家公司或哪一批公司设定的；它代表的是开盘那一刻买卖双方之间短暂的均衡，通常由盘前活动决定。举例来说，Emini 基本上是一个 24 小时市场，在纽约证券交易所开盘之前的几个小时里都在持续活跃地交易、从不间断。如果机构当天计划买入的量很大，市场为什么有时候会把股票开在昨天收盘价之上、先抛售一段，然后才涨到新高？如果你是机构交易员，今天有一大堆买单要成交，你会很乐意看到市场开在你想要买入的价格之上，然后急跌进入你的买入区，让你可以和其他机构一起激进买入——那些机构多半也从客户那里接到了大量类似的买单；接着你会希望看到一次小幅卖出高潮，形成一个有说服力的当天低点。看多的机构不买入，就造成了下跌真空，能把市场迅速吸进它们的买入区；这个买入区永远在某个支撑区，在那里它们会激进地、不停歇地买入，往往就此造出当天的低点。


> Why does the market make a big move over the first several bars and then reverse? Why doesn't it simply open at the low or high of the day? The location of the open of the day is not set by any firm or group of firms; instead, it represents a brief equilibrium between buyers and sellers at the instant of the open, and it is usually determined by the premarket activity. For example, the Emini is basically a 24-hour market and trades actively, uninterrupted, for hours leading up to the open of the New York Stock Exchange. If the institutions have a large amount of buying planned for the day, why would the market ever open a stock above yesterday's close and then sell off before rallying to a new high? If you were an institutional trader and had a lot of buy orders to fill today, you would love the market to open above where you wanted to buy and then have a sharp move down into your buy zone where you could aggressively buy along with all the other institutions that likely also have lots of similar buy orders from their clients; you would then hope to see a small sell climax that will form a convincing low of the day. The lack of buying by the bullish institutions creates a sell vacuum that can quickly suck the market down into their buy zone, which is always at an area of support, where they will buy aggressively and relentlessly, often creating the low of the day.


如果开盘时从那场卖出高潮反弹回来的反转足够强，愿意做空的交易者就会很少，因为大家普遍会觉得上涨动能强到足以保证在低点被回测（如果真被回测的话）之前，至少还会有第二段上涨行情。如果你是一名机构交易员，有没有什么办法能让这种情况发生？有！你可以在盘前时段的收盘阶段买入，把价格推上去，顺便成交一部分订单。在太平洋标准时间早上 6:30 开盘之前，推动股票价格并不需要那么大的成交量。然后，等市场一开盘，你就可以清掉一部分或全部多头，甚至还可以做一点空。既然你想在更低的价位买入，你就不会在市场跌到你所认为的值得买的位置之前开始买——那个位置会是一个支撑区。这就是真空效应。买盘就在那里，但如果他们认为几分钟后价格会更低，他们就会站到一边去。几分钟后就能更便宜地买到，为什么要现在买？看多的力量明明很强却没有人买，价格于是被迅速吸下去。一旦价格进入他们的买入区，他们看到了价值，也认为市场不会再跌多少。他们像是凭空冒出来一样，不停歇地买入，造成一次非常凌厉的多头反转。空头也会看到那个支撑；如果他们相信这段下跌行情可能已经结束，他们也会变成买家——在空单上止盈。


> If the reversal back up from that sell climax on the open is strong enough, very few traders will be looking to short, because there will be a general feeling that the upward momentum is sufficiently strong to warrant at least a second leg up before the low is tested, if it gets tested. Would there be anything that you, if you were an institutional trader, could do to make this happen? Yes! You could buy into the close of the premarket to push the price up and fill some of your orders. Not as much volume is needed in stocks to move the price before the 6:30 a.m. PST open. Then, once the market opens, you could liquidate some or all of your longs and even do some shorting. Since you want to buy lower, you will not start buying until the market falls to an area that you consider represents value, which will be at a support area. This is a vacuum effect. The buyers are there, but they will step aside if they think that the price will be lower in a few minutes. Why buy now if you can buy for less in a few minutes? This absence of buying despite the existence of very strong bulls allows the price to get sucked down quickly. Once it is in their buy zone, they see value and doubt the market will fall further. They appear as if out of nowhere and buy relentlessly, causing a very sharp bull reversal. The shorts will also see the support, and if they believe that the leg down is likely over, they, too, will become buyers as they take profits on their shorts.


价格行为非常重要。交易者想看到的是：当市场跌到某个关键支撑价位——比如均线、前一个波段高点或低点、昨天的低点，或者某条趋势线或趋势通道线——时，市场如何反应。多数交易是计算机完成的，它们用算法计算出这些支撑位在哪里。如果有足够多的公司依赖同样的支撑位，买盘就会压过卖盘，市场就会反转向上。事先不可能知道买盘会强到什么程度，但既然支撑总是基于数学算出来的，有经验的交易者通常能预判可能出现反转的区域，并做好下单准备。如果下跌动能开始减弱，市场开始从那个关键价位反转向上，机构就会清掉手里的空单，并激进买入以完成订单。由于多数公司持有类似的订单，市场就会开始上涨。如果一家公司认为当天的低点可能已经出现，它会随着市场上涨继续买入，并激进地买下每一次回调。由于它的订单规模巨大，它不想一次买完、冒着先急涨再出现买入高潮的风险。它更愿意整天都有条不紊地持续买入，直到所有订单成交为止。随着订单成交，这种不停歇的买入把市场推得更高，还会吸引动量交易者，他们同样会在全天不断买入，进一步加大买压。


> Price action is very important. A trader wants to see how the market responds once it gets down to some key support price, like the moving average, or a prior swing high or low, or the low of yesterday, or a trend line or trend channel line. Most of the trading is done by computers, which use algorithms to calculate where these support levels are. If enough firms are relying on the same support levels, the buying will overwhelm the selling and the market will reverse up. It is impossible to know in advance how strong the buying will be, but since the support is always based on mathematics, an experienced trader can usually anticipate areas where reversals might occur and be ready to place trades. If the downward momentum begins to wane and the market starts to reverse up from the key price, institutions will liquidate any shorts and aggressively buy to fill their orders. Since most firms will have similar orders, the market will start to rally. If a firm believes that the low of the day might be in, it will continue to buy as the market rallies and will aggressively buy any pullbacks. Since its order size is huge, it doesn't want to buy all at once and risk causing a spike up and then a buy climax. Instead, it would rather just keep buying in an orderly fashion all day long until all of its orders get filled. As they get filled, the relentless buying causes the market to go up more, which attracts momentum traders who will also buy throughout the day, adding to the buying pressure.


实际情况真是这样吗？机构里的交易者知道他们自己是不是这么做的，但从来没有人能确知市场在某个特定日子为什么会反转。反转背后的原因多得数不清，而这些原因并不重要。唯一重要的是价格行为。反转常常在报告发布几秒之后发生，但单靠看 CNBC，个体交易者不太可能弄懂市场会如何回应一份报告。面对利多或利空的报告，市场都可能上涨或抛售，而在没有价格行为的情况下，交易者根本没有能力可靠地解读一份报告。要知道市场会如何回应，最好的办法就是看它怎么回应，并随着价格行为的展开下单。很多时候，报告前的那根K线就是一个极好的建仓形态，会在报告发布时被触发。如果你觉得非要在报告发布时交易，那就下好订单和止损，然后相信自己的判读。由于报告发布时的滑点可能很大，几乎总是等到报告发布之后再交易更好。如果你在报告发布时入场，你可能会发现入场时多了几个最小报价单位的滑点，接着市场猛烈反转，出场时又多了额外的滑点。你以为风险是八个最小报价单位的一笔交易，结果亏了 16 个或更多最小报价单位。如果你交易的是流动性更稀薄的市场，滑点可能严重得多，你在头一个小时里亏得太多，到收盘都回不到保本。


> Is this what actually happens? Traders at institutions know if this is what they do, but no one ever knows for certain why the market reverses on any given day. The reversal is due to countless reasons, but those reasons are irrelevant. All that matters is price action. Reversals often happen seconds after a report is released, but an individual trader is unlikely to understand how the market will respond to a report by simply watching CNBC. The market can rally or sell off in response to either a bullish or a bearish report, and a trader is simply not qualified to reliably interpret a report in the absence of price action. The best way to know how the market will respond is simply to watch it respond and place your trades as the price action unfolds. Very often, the bar before the report is a great setup that gets triggered on the report. If you feel compelled to trade on the release of the report, place your order and then your stop and trust your read. Since slippage can be significant on a report, it is almost always better to wait until after the report is released. If you enter on the report, you might find that you got a few ticks of slippage on the entry, and then the market violently reverses and you get additional slippage on your exit. What you thought was a trade with a risk of eight ticks ends up as a trade where you lost 16 or more ticks. If you trade thinner markets, your slippage could be much worse and you could be so far down in the first hour that you will not get back to breakeven by the close.


当市场因为太平洋标准时间早上 7:00 的报告而急涨时，通常是因为机构本来就打算买入，只是希望买得更低。当报告看起来足够利多，让他们相信自己没法在更低的价位成交时，他们就在报告发布时买入了。如果他们要买的量足够大，就会整天持续买入，这一天也就变成了多头趋势日。反过来，如果它们最初的买盘被另一些机构压过——那些机构本来盼着一波上涨、好在更高的价位做空——那么向上突破就会失败，市场转为下跌。这些空头此前是看不见的，因为他们在等一波上涨来做空；只有当它们开始激进地做空这波上涨、把市场打回去时，它们的力量才显现出来。显然，还有无数其他因素一直在起作用，而且存在体量巨大的动量交易者，他们对报告没有任何看法，只是在行情展开时顺着方向重仓交易。不过，机构在报告发布前就持有的偏向是一个重要组成部分。机构在报告发布之前就已经知道自己想做什么，尽管如果报告完全出乎意料，每家都会有应对预案。


> When the market rallies sharply on a 7:00 a.m. PST report, it is usually because the institutions were already planning on buying, but were hoping to buy lower. When the report appeared sufficiently bullish for them to believe that they would not be able to fill their orders lower, they bought on the report. If they have enough buying to do, they will continue to buy all day, and the day will become a bull trend day. If, on the other hand, their initial buying is overwhelmed by other institutions who were hoping for a rally that would allow them to short at a higher price, the upside breakout will fail and the market will trend down. These bears were invisible because they were waiting for a rally to short and their power became evident only once they began to aggressively short the rally and turn the market back down. Obviously, countless other factors are always in play, and there are huge momentum traders who have no opinion about a report and simply trade heavily in the direction of the move as it is unfolding. However, the institutional bias going into the report is an important component. The institutions already knew what they wanted to do before the report was released, although all would have contingencies if the report was a complete surprise.


全部交易中大约 70% 是自动化的，而这种由计算机生成的买卖会越来越重要。道琼斯公司现在有一项名为 Lexicon 的新闻服务，向订户传送机器可读的财经新闻。Lexicon 会扫描道琼斯所有关于股票的报道，把信息转换成算法可以用来做决策的形式，让它们在几分之一秒内决定买入或卖出股票。其中一些算法依据的是报告里的基本面数据。上个月新增了多少个就业岗位？核心消费者价格指数（CPI）是多少？债券拍卖的认购倍数是多少？另一些算法在更长的时间级别上运行，除了新闻推送之外，还会分析股票表现和财报，据此做出交易决策。还有一些算法纯属统计性质，比如：如果 Emini 上涨了 10 个最小报价单位、而且其间最多只回调了一个最小报价单位，那就用市价买入，赚两个最小报价单位后出场。另一家公司可能找到一个统计上的理由，去把这波上涨空下来、赚三个最小报价单位。谁也无法知道哪家公司在做什么，但如果有人能想出一个点子，并且经过检验发现它在数学上站得住脚，那么他们的计算机很可能已经在用它交易了。有些公司的算法可能是基本面与统计方法的混合体。也许经济数据利好时程序会立刻买入，但如果它们有统计证据表明，在这个特定的经济数据上 Emini 上涨三个点之后会反转到新低，那么程序可能会先止盈，甚至反手做一笔剥头皮。


> About 70 percent of all trading is automated, and this computer-generated buying and selling will become increasingly important. Dow Jones & Company now has a news service called Lexicon that transmits machine-readable financial news to its subscribers. Lexicon scans all of the Dow Jones stories about stocks and converts the information into a form that the algorithms can use to make decisions to buy and sell stocks in a fraction of a second. Some of the algorithms are based on the fundamental components in the report. How many new jobs were created last month? What was the core consumer price index (CPI)? What was the bid-to-cover ratio in the bond auction? Other algorithms operate on a longer time frame and analyze stock performance and earnings statements, in addition to the news feeds, to make trading decisions. Still other algorithms are purely statistical, like if the Emini rallied 10 ticks without at most a one-tick pullback, then buy at the market and exit with a two-tick profit. Another firm might find a statistical reason to short that rally for a three-tick profit. It is impossible to know what any firm is doing, but if someone can think of an idea and it can be tested and found to be mathematically sound, their computers are probably trading it. Some firms might have algorithms that are hybrids of the fundamental and statistical approaches. Maybe if the economic number is favorable, the programs will buy immediately, but if they have statistical evidence that tells them that the Emini will then reverse to a new low after rallying three points on this particular economic number, the program might take profits and even reverse for a scalp.


有些程序使用差分进化优化软件生成数据，再用这些数据生成其他数据。它们可以不断优化这些数据，直到达到某种数学上的确定性，然后用结果自动买入或卖出股票。有些订单大得需要花时间下，算法交易软件会把订单拆成小块，以免那些想从正在形成的趋势中获利的交易者察觉到这笔交易。掠夺性交易算法则试图破解算法交易程序想要隐藏的东西。人人都在寻找优势，越来越多的公司在用计算机寻找优势并下单。


> Some programs use differential evolution optimizing software to generate data that is used to generate other data. They can continue to refine the data until it reaches some level of mathematical certainty, and then the result is used to automatically buy or sell stocks. Some orders are so huge that they take time to place, and algorithmic trading software breaks the orders into small pieces to conceal the trading from traders who would try to capitalize on the incipient trend. Predatory trading algorithms try to unravel what the algorithm trading programs are trying to hide. Everyone is looking for an edge, and more and more firms are using computers to find the edges and place the trades.


既然计算机分析数据、下单的速度远快于交易者，而且它们跑的是具有数学优势的程序，那么想在报告发布的那一刻和它们竞争就是一件必亏的事。这些都是性能极高的计算机，而且就放在离交易所非常近的地方，能在几分之一秒内成交巨额成交量。结果是价格变动常常快到根本读不过来。事实上，价格变动可能快到你在家里的计算机看到的情况比实际发生的事情晚好几秒。太多时候，头一两秒里的行情幅度非常大，几秒之后却反转了，然后可能再次反转。交易者根本无法足够快地做决定和下单，从而在这种局面里盈利。更好的做法是等一等，看报告是否带来一段明确的始终入场走势，然后顺着那个方向交易。当你的对手对你有优势时——在这里是速度优势——最好等它们的优势消失之后再交易。多数交易者不该在报告发布后的那几秒里交易，而应该等价格行为恢复到正常状态，这往往需要一分钟到 10 分钟左右。


> Since computers can analyze the data and place trades far faster than a trader can, and the computers are running programs that have a mathematical edge, it is a losing proposition to try to compete with them at the moment a report is released. These are very high-powered computers and are located very close to the exchanges, and can trade huge volumes in a fraction of a second. The result is price movement that is often too fast to read. In fact, the price movement can be so fast that your computer at home may be several seconds behind what is actually taking place. Too often the moves are very large in the first second or two, only to reverse a few seconds later, and then maybe reverse again. Traders simply cannot make decisions and place orders fast enough to trade this situation profitably. It is better to wait to see if a clear always-in move comes from the report and then trade in that direction. When your opponents have an edge over you—in this case, speed —it is better to wait for their edge to disappear before trading again. Most traders should not trade in the seconds after a report but should wait for the price action to return to normal, which often takes one to about 10 minutes.


没有人能事先知道，所有大机构买单的总和，是否足以压过那些想做空的机构，也不知道空头代表的资金是不是多得多、足以把市场压下去。在大多数交易日里，多头和空头会先你来我往一阵子，多头持续买入，空头持续卖出。市场在上涨真空和下跌真空之间上下试探，等待着某一方在市场走到极值时有能力控制住盘面。当价格足够低时，一直在等市场跌到他们眼中价值区的强劲多头会激进买入。市场随后快速涨到多头不再觉得价格有吸引力的区域，他们停止买入并开始止盈。一直在等更高价位卖出的强劲空头，则会凭空冒出来，激进做空。到了某个时点，某一方认定自己不愿在当前位置继续激进交易，这就造成了失衡，让另一方开始把市场推向他们的方向。输的一方开始平仓，这又给趋势添了一把火。赢的一方看到市场朝着自己的方向走，就加仓，趋势因此更强。到了某个时点，他们会开始止盈，这就带来一次回调。一旦市场回落到对这些公司来说重新具有价值的位置，它们就会再次加仓，结果通常就是对趋势极值的一次回测。


> No one knows in advance whether the sum total of all the buy orders at all of the major institutions would be enough to overwhelm the institutions that were looking to short, or whether the shorts represented vastly more dollars and would be able to drive the market down. On most days, the action is two-sided for a while as the bulls continue to buy and the bears continue to sell. The market probes up and down in buy and sell vacuums, looking for one side to take control over the market when the market reaches an extreme. When it is low enough, strong bulls, who have been waiting for the market to reach a level that they see as value, will buy aggressively. The market then races up to an area where the bulls no longer feel that the price represents good value, and they stop buying and begin to take profits. The strong bears, who have been waiting for higher prices to sell, appear out of nowhere and short aggressively. At some point, one side decides that they are unwilling to continue trading aggressively at the current price, and this creates an imbalance that allows the other side to begin to move the market in their direction. The losing side begins to cover, and this adds to the trend. The winning side sees the market moving their way and they add to their positions, creating a stronger trend. At some point, they will begin to take profits and this will result in a pullback. Once the market comes back far enough to represent value to these firms, they will once again begin to add to their positions and the result will usually be a test of the trend's extreme.


经济报告发布时，急剧反转很常见；这些反转你可能看不懂，但那并不重要。一份利多的报告怎么会先带来一波上涨，几秒钟之后又跟着创出当天新低？如果几分钟前市场还那么看跌，现在怎么又会这么看多？别去琢磨这些。你只需要寻找标准的价格行为建仓形态，然后不加思索地照做，完全不用考虑这次反转为什么发生。你只需要知道它确实正在发生，而你必须入场。你不需要理解它，但有一点很重要：它可能发生得很快，你可能反应不够快，从而亏钱。


> Sharp reversals are common on economic reports, and the reversals may not make sense to you, but that is irrelevant. How can a bullish report lead to a rally and then seconds later be followed by a new low of the day? If the market was so bearish a couple of minutes ago, how can it be so bullish now? Don't give it any thought. Instead, just look for standard price action setups and trade them mindlessly without giving any consideration to the reasons why the reversal is taking place. All that you need to know is that it is in fact taking place and you must enter. You don't need to understand it, but it is important to realize that it can happen quickly and you might not react fast enough to avoid losing money.


虽然 5分钟图最容易读懂、也最可靠，但 3分钟图同样交易得不错，尤其是在头一个小时里。不过，3分钟图更容易出现亏损交易；如果你想要最高的胜率、不想承受亏损带来的负面情绪，就应该坚持交易 5分钟图，并着手提高自己的仓位规模。


> Although the 5 minute chart is the easiest to read and the most reliable, the 3 minute chart trades well, particularly in the first hour. However, it is prone to more losers, and if you like the highest winning percentage and don't want the negative emotion that comes from losing, you should stick to trading the 5 minute chart and work on increasing your position size.


作为交易者，最好把分析保持得简单，尤其是在市场走得很快的头一个小时里。绝大多数开盘都与前一天最后一小时左右的价格行为有关，表现为突破、突破失败、突破回调，或者开盘即趋势，而这些形态中的任何一种都可能走得非常快。


> As a trader, it is best to keep your analysis simple, especially in the first hour when the market is moving quickly. The vast majority of opens are related to the price action of the final hour or so of the prior day and take the form of a breakout, a failed breakout, a breakout pullback, or a trend from the open, and any of these can move very fast.


日内交易最难的地方之一，是保持专注。多数交易者根本没法整场都高度绷紧地盯住市场，他们会被无聊和分心击倒，并且常常怀疑这是自己无法持续稳定盈利的主要障碍。他们想得没错。头一个小时给了你一个弥补这个问题的好机会。即使你认为自己一整天盯住每一笔成交、或者至少每一根 5分钟K线是不可能的，你也许会相信自己能坚持一个小时。这必须成为你的主要目标之一，因为这是赚钱的好办法。头一个小时的成交量巨大，每天都有好几笔交易。如果你只做头一个小时，并且在做到持续稳定盈利之后加大仓位规模，你可能会发现，只有那一个小时需要高度紧绷。接下来一天里的其余时间，你只需要找两三次主要趋势反转——这些反转几乎总是能提前 10 分钟或更久预判出来，尤其是当你在等待二次入场的时候（一看到第一次入场出现，就准备好接第二次，它通常会在几根K线之内到来）。等你能把头一个小时交易好了，再去做头两个小时，那通常是一天里最好的交易时段，而且常常能给你带来你期望从一整天里得到的所有利润。


> One of the most difficult aspects of day trading is maintaining focus. Most traders simply cannot stay intensely connected to the market for the entire session, and they succumb to boredom and distractions and often suspect that this is a major obstacle to them becoming consistently profitable. And they are right. The first hour provides you with a great opportunity to remedy this problem. Even if you think that watching every tick or at least every 5 minute bar is impossible for you for an entire day, you might believe that you can do it for an hour. This has to become one of your primary goals because it is a great way to make money. The volume is huge and there are several trades every day in that first hour. If you simply trade the first hour and increase your position size once you become consistently profitable, you might discover that the intensity is needed for only that hour. Then, for the rest of the day, just look for two or three major reversals, which you can almost always anticipate 10 or more minutes in advance, especially if you are waiting for second entries (once you see the first one, get ready to take the second, which will usually follow within a few bars). Once you can trade the first hour well, look to trade the first two hours, which usually provide the best trading of the day and can very often give you all of the profit that you expect from the entire day.


在圣诞节那周、7 月 4 日那周这样的假期前后交易时，头一个小时往往非常重要，因为那常常是市场表现得像平常日子的唯一时段。之后市场经常会在当天余下的时间里进入窄幅交易区间。如果你想在假期前后交易，就必须对头一个小时里的建仓形态格外警觉。


> When trading around holidays like Christmas week and the week of the Fourth of July, the first hour is often very important because often that is the only time when the market behaves like a normal day. It then frequently enters a tight trading range for the rest of the day. If you want to trade around holidays, you have to be particularly alert to setups in the first hour.


在交易 5分钟图时，很容易忘记还有很多机构交易者同时也在关注 15分钟图。第一根 15分钟K线在第三根 5分钟K线收盘时收盘，因此第三根K线附近的活动会影响第一根 15分钟K线的样子。举例来说，如果当天前两根K线朝一个方向走，然后第三根是一根较小的停顿K线，那么这根K线的突破就会决定 15分钟图上出现的是突破还是失败形态。因此，交易当天第三根K线的突破，往往会带来一段大行情。在大多数交易日里，不要单凭第三根K线就下单，但要意识到它额外的意义。如果它是一根重要的K线，通常还会有其他价格行为来支持这笔交易，而那些额外信息才应该是下单的依据。


> When trading the 5 minute chart, it is easy to not be thinking about the many institutional traders who are also paying attention to 15 minute charts. The first 15 minute bar closes at the close of the third 5 minute bar and therefore activity around this third bar will influence the appearance of the first 15 minute bar. For example, if the first two bars of the day move in one direction and then the third bar is a smaller pause bar, the breakout of the bar will determine whether there is a 15 minute breakout or there could be a failure. Therefore, trading the breakout of the third bar of the day often leads to a big move. Do not place a trade on the third bar alone on most days, but be aware of its extra significance. If it is an important bar, there will usually be other price action to support the trade, and that additional information should be the basis for the trade.


类似的逻辑也可以用在 30分钟图和 60分钟图的最后一根 5分钟K线上（例如，60分钟图由 12 根 5分钟K线组成，所以最后一根 5分钟K线收盘时，60分钟K线也同时收盘）；不过，把注意力放在这么长的时间级别及其并不频繁的入场机会上，会增加错过一笔或多笔盈利的 5分钟交易的可能性，因此并不值得。


> Similar logic can also be used for the last 5 minute bar of the 30 and 60 minute charts (for example, the 60 minute chart is made of 12 bars on the 5 minute chart, so the final one closes when the 60 minute bar closes), but focusing on such longer time frames and their infrequent entries increases the chances of missing one or more profitable 5 minute trades and therefore is not worthwhile.


铁丝网代表双向交易；当它在头一个小时里形成时，之后这一天往往是多头和空头轮流控制市场。如果铁丝网之后出现趋势，那么某个时点通常会出现一个可以做交易的逆势建仓形态。


> Barbwire represents two-sided trading, and when it develops in the first hour, it often will be followed by a day where bulls and bears alternate control of the market. If there is a trend after the barbwire, there will usually be a tradable countertrend setup at some point.


当天的第一根K线往往能显示这一天会是什么样子。如果它是昨天最后一小时那段窄幅交易区间中部的一根十字星，而且均线走平，那么这一天更可能是交易区间日。如果这根K线是一根趋势K线，却带着显眼的影线，那它就是一个单K线的交易区间。由于多数交易区间的突破都会失败，市场很可能没法在这根K线上方或下方走出一两根K线以上，就会出现反转。有些交易者在第一根K线影线显眼时，会反向操作它的突破，并分一两次建仓。举例来说，不论市场是向上跳空还是向下跳空，也不论K线的实体是阳是阴，只要影线相当显眼，许多交易者就会在这根K线上方做空、在下方做多来剥头皮，因为他们知道头一个小时里通常是反转占主导，而交易区间的突破——哪怕这个交易区间只是一根K线——很可能失败。于是他们押注它会失败，朝反方向交易。由于他们把那根K线看成一个单K线交易区间，他们就处在交易区间模式里，这意味着通常会把仓位的大部分或全部拿来剥头皮。


> The first bar of the day often shows what the day will be like. If it is a doji in the middle of a tight trading range from the final hour of yesterday and the moving average is flat, the odds favor a trading range day. If the bar is a trend bar but has prominent tails, it is a one-bar trading range. Since most trading range breakouts fail, the market will probably not be able to move above or below the bar for more than a bar or two before there is a reversal. Some traders fade the breakouts of the first bar if it has prominent tails, and they will scale in once or twice. For example, whether the market gaps up or down or has a bull or bear body, if the tails are fairly prominent, many traders will short above the bar and buy below the bar for a scalp, since they know that reversals usually dominate the first hour and that the breakout of a trading range, even if the trading range is a single bar, is likely to fail. Therefore, they bet that it will fail and trade in the opposite direction. Since they see that bar as a one-bar trading range, they are in trading range mode, which means that they will usually scalp most or all of their position.


接下来的几根K线也能显示这一天的偏向。如果十字星接连出现，而且头一个小时里有五次反转，那么是交易区间日的可能性就更高。如果有大幅跳空开盘，而且市场在前四根K线上走出趋势，那很可能就是趋势日。交易者会为第一根K线就走出的趋势做好准备；这些开头的K线可能就是「急速与通道」型趋势日里那段急速行情。不过，他们也会准备好应对第一次回调变成一小面最终旗形的情形。这可能引出反方向的急速行情、对开盘区间另一端的突破，然后是一段反方向的趋势。


> The next several bars can also show the bias of the day. If dojis continue and there are five reversals in the first hour, the odds of a trading range day go up. If there is a large gap opening and the market trends for the first four bars, the odds of a trend day are good. Traders will be ready for a trend from the first bar trend, and those first bars might be the spike of a spike and channel trend day. However, they will be ready if the first pullback becomes a small final flag. This can lead to a spike in the opposite direction, a breakout of the opposite end of the opening range, and then a trend in the opposite direction.


头一两个小时里最强的波段交易来自多个形态的叠加，但这些形态有时并不明显；交易者应该在开盘前就留意它们，并想清楚可能会发生什么。对任何事情都要同时考虑看多和看空两种情形，因为两边都有聪明钱。一如既往，交易者要找的是突破和突破失败。举例来说，昨天尾盘是不是有一段长达 18 根K线的熊旗，并回调到空头趋势线？如果是，今天是不是刚好开在这面熊旗下方、也开在均线下方，形成了对这面旗形的突破，随后却上涨了两根K线、到达均线并在那里形成一根空头反转K线？如果是这样，这就是均线处的一次向下开盘反转，也是在回测空头趋势线之后的突破回调做空，而且信号K线不错，构成一个高概率的波段（同时也是剥头皮）做空机会。出现的因素越多，概率就越高；一旦某个波段建仓形态有了高概率，它就是非常强的建仓形态。或者换一种情形：昨天是不是以一个 25 根K线长的交易区间向上突破收尾，而那段交易区间处在一段呈楔形、已经走了三天的弱势多头趋势之中？市场当时是不是正处在一个为期两周的交易区间顶部附近？那次突破是不是有两段上涨行情，市场是不是收在那段三天楔形上涨行情上方的趋势通道线处？如果是，今天是不是开在昨天收盘价下方几个最小报价单位处，先涨了一段，然后向下反转、形成一根强劲的空头反转K线，从而在「向上突破昨天的高点与那个交易区间（很可能是最终旗形）失败」以及「位于楔形多头通道顶部之上」这两个条件下给出二次入场卖出信号？如果是这样，这就是一个高概率的波段（同时也是剥头皮）做空机会。


> The strongest swing trades in the first couple of hours come from a confluence of patterns, but the patterns are sometimes subtle and traders should look for them before the open and think about what might happen. Always consider both the bull and bear case for everything, because there is smart money on both sides. As always, traders are looking for breakouts and failed breakouts. For example, was there an 18-bar long bear flag at the end of yesterday that pulled back to the bear trend line, and if so, did today open just below the bear flag and below the moving average, creating a breakout of the flag, but then rally for two bars to the moving average where it formed a bear reversal bar? If so, this is an opening reversal down at the moving average and a breakout pullback short, after a test of the bear trend line, with a good signal bar, creating a high probability swing (and scalp) short. The more factors that are present, the higher the probability, and when there is a swing setup with a high probability, the setup is very strong. Alternatively, did yesterday end with a bull breakout from a 25-bar long trading range in a three day weak bull trend that had a wedge shape, and was the market near the top of a two week long trading range, and did the breakout have two legs up and did the market close at the trend channel line above the three day wedge rally? Is so, did today open a few ticks below the close of yesterday, trade up, and then reverse down into a strong bear reversal bar, creating a second entry sell signal on the failed breakout above yesterday's high and the trading range (a likely final flag) and above the top of the wedge bull channel? If so, this is a high probability swing (and scalp) short.


![图 PIII.1](figures/fig-PIII-1.jpg)


**图 PIII.1　早盘反转失败**


市场常常在开头几根K线之后突然反转，但永远要做好准备，反转可能失败并形成突破回调。如图 PIII.1 所示，第1根K线是当天的第三根K线，是一根小的多头反转K线。它从均线以及昨天的一个波段低点处反转向上。这是一个很好的开盘反转做多入场点，也使得第一根 15分钟K线没有成为一根强劲的空头趋势K线。


> The market often abruptly reverses after the first few bars, but always be prepared for the reversal to fail and set up a breakout pullback. As shown in Figure PIII.1, bar 1 was the third bar of the day and it was a small bull reversal bar. It reversed up from the moving average and a swing low from yesterday. This was a great opening reversal long entry, and it also prevented the first 15 minute bar from being a strong bear trend bar.


从第1根K线开始，市场连续走出四根多头趋势K线。在第二根之后，一些多头开始在前一根K线的低点挂买入限价单，因为他们预期第一次向下反转的尝试会失败。结果他们是在第2根K线之后又过了三根K线才形成的那根小空头K线上成交的。


> The market had four consecutive bull trend bars starting at bar 1. After the second one, some bulls started placing buy limit orders at the low of the prior bar, expecting the first attempt to reverse down to fail. They were filled on the small bear bar that formed three bars after bar 2.


第二天，第3根K线也反转了前一天的一个波段低点，并带来了一次够剥头皮的利润，但那根多头入场K线向下反转，形成一次两根K线反转的做空入场。注意，第3根K线是一根空头趋势K线，而不是一根强劲的反转K线，所以这算不上一个好的逆势做多建仓形态。多头原本期待一次楔形反转，其中前两次推进发生在昨天最后几个小时里。然而，第3根K线和它前面那根都是小小的交易区间K线。这两根K线太小，缺少足够的多头力量，几乎没有机会反转那波强劲抛售。多头试图在第3根K线之后的下一根K线上制造出这种力量，但空头用一根更大的空头趋势K线迅速把市场打了下去。


> The next day, bar 3 also reversed a swing low from the day before and led to a scalper's profit, but the bull entry bar reversed down in a two-bar reversal for a short entry. Note that bar 3 was a bear trend bar and not a strong reversal bar, so this was not a good countertrend long setup. The bulls were hoping for a wedge reversal, where the first two pushes occurred in the final couple of hours of yesterday. However, bar 3 and the bar before it were small trading range bars. The bars were too small and lacked sufficient bullish strength to have much chance of reversing that strong sell-off. The bulls tried to create that strength on the bar after bar 3, but the bears quickly reversed the market down with an even larger bear trend bar.


跌破第3根K线的低点，同时也是在一个大幅向下跳空的日子里跌破当天的第一根 15分钟K线，这提高了出现一段可交易下跌波段行情的可能性。


> The break below the bar 3 low was also a break below the first 15 minute bar of the day on a day with a large gap down, increasing the odds of a tradable downswing.


注意，昨天的收盘价刚好低于开盘价，并且明显低于当天的高点。这就在日线图上形成了一根反转K线，尽管它的阳线实体很小。有些看日线图交易的交易者，会在今天跌破昨天低点时挂卖出止损单去做空。由于在那个位置下方有那么多交易者愿意卖出，今天市场向下跳空，并在第一根K线上就跌破了昨天的低点，触发了日线图上的卖出信号。这次突破在第3根K线处差点走成失败形态，但反转向上的尝试失败了，结果形成双顶熊旗和突破回调做空，入场点在第4根K线两根K线反转的下方。
**图 PIII.2　最初几根K线可以定下全天的基调**如图 PIII.2 所示，开头几根K线里的价格行为往往预示了后面会发生什么。从开盘到第4根K线之前那根K线的这波上涨行情里有好几根大阳线，只有两根小阴线，说明多头愿意激进交易。这一点在当天晚些时候应该记住，以防再出现做多的建仓形态。心里装着这一点，交易者就该更愿意把多头仓位的一部分拿成波段，因为趋势更有可能延续下去。


> Notice that yesterday's close was just below its open and well below the high of the day. This created a reversal bar on the daily chart, even though it had a small bull body. Some traders who trade off of the daily chart would then have placed sell stops to go short if today fell below yesterday's low. Because there were so many traders willing to sell down there, the market gapped down today and traded below yesterday's low on the first bar, triggering the sell signal on the daily chart. The breakout attempted to fail at bar 3, but the reversal up failed and created a double top bear flag and breakout pullback short, with an entry below the bar 4 two-bar reversal. FIGURE PIII.2 The First Few Bars Can Set the Tone As shown in Figure PIII.2, the price action in the first several bars often foreshadows what happens later. The rally from the open to the bar before bar 4 had several large bull bars and only two small bear bars, showing that the bulls were willing to be aggressive. This was something to remember later in the day in case another buy setup appeared. Keeping that in mind, traders should have been more willing to swing part of their longs because the trend was more likely to resume.


当天的高点通常来自某种双顶，而这种双顶很少看起来像双顶。在这里，第6根K线是第二次向上测试的终点，因此是做空双顶的信号。第4根K线则成为可能的当天高点。第8根K线与昨天的收盘低点构成一个双底，并形成了今天的低点。尽管开盘反转上做成一波段的概率可能只有 40%，但许多这类交易的结果是小赚或小亏。这些小交易通常相互抵消，而达到四个点或更多的那 40% 就成了交易者利润的来源。对多数交易者来说，在他们尝试把日内交易做成一项事业的过程中，交易这些开盘后的行情应该是一块基石。


> The high of the day usually comes from some kind of double top that rarely looks like a double top. Here, bar 6 was the end of a second test up and therefore was the signal for a double top short. Bar 4 became the possible high of the day. Bar 8 was a double bottom with the closing low of yesterday, and it formed the low of today. Even though the probability of a successful swing on an opening reversal might be only 40 percent, many of the trades result in a small profit or a small loss. These small trades usually balance out, and the 40 percent that reach four or more points become the source of a trader's profit. Trading these opening moves should be a cornerstone for most traders as they try to build a business in day trading.


有经验的剥头皮交易者预期多数突破尝试都会失败，并在头一两个小时里着眼于低买高卖。可做的剥头皮包括：在第一根K线（它是一根十字星K线）上方卖出，并在更高处分批建仓（第一次入场保本出场，第二、第三次入场获利出场）；在第1根多头趋势K线上方买入；在第2根K线之后那根空头内包K线下方做空（那是对昨天交易区间向上突破的失败）；在第3根K线突破前一根K线高点时买入（因为涨到第2根K线的那段急速行情很强，后面很可能跟着第二段上涨行情）；在第3根K线突破创出当天新高之后出现的那次两根K线反转下方做空（低2做空）；以及在「对跌到第5根K线的空头微型通道的突破已经走了两段」之后，于第6根多头趋势K线下方做空，因为跌到第5根K线的那段强劲空头微型通道的底部很可能被回测。


> Experienced scalpers expect most breakout attempts to fail, and look to buy low and sell high in the first hour or two. Possible scalps included: selling above the first bar, which was a doji bar, and scaling in higher (exiting the first entry at breakeven and the second and third entries with a profit); buying above the bar 1 bull trend bar; shorting below the bear inside bar that followed bar 2 (a failed breakout above the trading range of yesterday); buying on bar 3 as it broke above the high of the prior bar (since the spike up to bar 2 was strong and was likely to be followed by a second leg up); shorting below the two-bar reversal that followed the bar 3 breakout to a new high of the day (a low 2 short); and shorting below the bar 6 bull trend bar, since it was a two-legged breakout of the bear micro channel down to bar 5 and the bottom of the strong bear micro channel down to bar 5 was likely to be tested.


第8根K线是第二次尝试反转「创出当天新低的突破」并取得了成功，而且它与昨天的收盘价构成一个双底，因此很可能引出一段至少包含两次上涨行情的行情。事实上，这段两段式上涨行情中间只有一次小小的横盘停顿，所以大部分上涨是在通道里完成的。当一段上涨行情主要在通道里完成时，即使中间有一次停顿和一小段第二段行情，多数交易者也会把整段通道看作第一段行情，并期待之后出现一段更明显的第二段行情。涨到第11根K线的那段上涨只是这条通道的延伸，其间没有明显回调，因此许多交易者会把从第8根K线到第11根K线的上涨看作仅仅一段行情。不过，和大多数通道一样，这里有大量相互重叠的K线、显眼的影线和空头趋势K线。多头通道就是熊旗，所以交易者都在等待向下突破，而这可能带来一次足够大的回调，让交易者相信第一段上涨显然已经结束。接下来他们就得判断：是第二段上涨仍然可能出现，还是这次修正已经持续得足够久，让空头觉得市场不会再涨多少，从而确信这是一个可以再次激进做空的好价位。市场并没有向下突破，而是强势向上突破，那些在过去几个小时里一直在做空的空头不得不迅速买回自己的空单。多头看到了这段多头急速行情有多强，于是一路用市价买入，因为当急速行情这么强时，更高的价格更有可能出现。


> Bar 8 was a successful second attempt to reverse the breakout to a new low of the day and a double bottom with the close of yesterday, so it was likely to lead to a rally that had at least two legs. In fact, the two-legged rally only had a small sideways pause and therefore the move up was mostly in a channel. When a rally is mostly in a channel, even if there is a pause and a small second leg, most traders will see the entire channel as the first leg and expect a more obvious second leg to follow. The move up to bar 11 was just an extension of that channel with no significant pullback, and therefore many traders would have considered the rally from bar 8 to bar 11 to be just one leg. However, as with most channels, there were many overlapping bars, prominent tails, and bear trend bars. A bull channel is a bear flag, so traders were looking for a downside breakout, which could have led to a pullback that was large enough to make traders believe that the first leg up was clearly over. They then needed to decide whether a second leg up was still likely or the correction had lasted long enough for the bears to feel that the market would not go much higher, thereby convincing them that this was a good price level to again aggressively short. Instead of breaking to the downside, the market broke strongly to the upside and the bears who had been shorting for the past couple of hours had to quickly buy back their shorts. The bulls saw how strong the bull spike was, and they bought at the market all of the way up because when a spike is this strong, the odds favor higher prices.


第12根K线是一个高2买点，对应的是第二段更大的上涨行情，而这段行情本身也包含两段更小的行情。


> Bar 12 was a high 2 buy for a second larger leg up, which also had two smaller legs.


![图 PIII.3](figures/fig-PIII-3.jpg)


**图 PIII.3　不要对波动幅度很小的股票做剥头皮**


交易者不该经常对日均波动幅度不到一美元的股票做剥头皮，但价格行为入场点仍然有效。如图 PIII.3 所示，英特尔（INTC）在头 15 分钟里出现两根大的空头趋势K线，随后形成双顶熊旗（第3根和第5根K线）。这是一个可靠的形态，往往会引出空头趋势日；在这里它引出的是一段「急速行情与高潮」式的空头趋势。昨天的多头趋势太强，所以今天的两段式下跌在第6根K线处反转向上——很可能是在 15分钟图或 60分钟图的均线处——但这波下跌至少够做一笔 10 美分的剥头皮。


> Traders should not often scalp stocks with average daily ranges under a dollar, but price action entries still work. As shown in Figure PIII.3, Intel (INTC) had two large bear trend bars in the first 15 minutes and then formed a double top bear flag (bars 3 and 5). This is a reliable pattern that often leads to a bear trend day, and here it led to a spike and climax bear trend. Yesterday's bull trend was so strong that today's two-legged selling reversed back up at bar 6, likely at the moving average on the 15 or 60 minute charts, but it was good for at least a 10 cent scalp.


只要均线像昨天那样陡峭向上，任何跌破它的强劲抛售几乎总会被一波可交易的反弹拉回去。第6根K线是与昨天 11:35 那波回调（它来自一段强劲上涨的急速行情）构成双底牛旗的信号。随后市场走出一段更强的多头急速行情直到收盘，整段上涨就变成了一段「急速行情与高潮」式的多头趋势。由于第二段急速行情相当于传统「急速与通道」型多头趋势里的通道部分，它的底部通常会被回测——这里就是如此。


> Whenever the moving average is as steeply up as it was yesterday, any strong sell-off below it will almost always be followed by a tradable rally back up. Bar 6 was the signal for a double bottom bull flag with yesterday's 11:35 pullback from a strong spike up. It then formed an even stronger bull spike into the close and the entire move up became a spike and climax bull trend. Since the second spike is comparable to the channel in a traditional spike and channel bull trend, its bottom usually gets tested, as it did here.


![图 PIII.4](figures/fig-PIII-4.jpg)


**图 PIII.4　早盘铁丝网往往导致交易区间日**


铁丝网式的走势（带大影线、大K线的窄幅交易区间）——当天头 90 分钟里出现显眼的影线、相互重叠的K线和多次反转——是剧烈双向交易和不确定性的标志，这一天通常会成为交易区间日。如图 PIII.4 所示，今天是趋势性交易区间日，但由于市场收在上方交易区间的顶部，它同时也是一个多头反转日。


> Barbwire type (tight trading range with big tails and big bars) of trading with prominent tails, overlapping bars, and many reversals for the first 90 minutes of the day is a sign of intense two-sided trading and uncertainty, and the day usually becomes a trading range day. As shown in Figure PIII.4, today was a trending trading range day, but since the market closed at the top of the upper trading range, it was also a bull reversal day.


当铁丝网在开盘时形成，通常意味着当天某个时点会出现两个方向上都可交易的波段行情。到当天第三根K线时，铁丝网形态已经初具可能：它的波动幅度大约有一半被前一根K线覆盖，而且它收在中部，这意味着下一根K线也很可能覆盖它大约一半的幅度。铁丝网一路持续贯穿了直到第2根K线的整段弱势上涨行情。之后是空头趋势线被突破、一个更低的高点，然后在第4根K线处形成对那个更低的高点的二次入场——它与第3根K线构成双顶。随后几根K线里的向下突破，使得趋势性交易区间成为可能，尤其是因为到此为止的波动幅度只有最近几天的一半略多一点，而且在急速行情之后很可能在下跌通道中扩大。交易者期待向下突破，然后是一段向下的等距运动，用来做他们的空头波段。向下突破使市场进入始终做空状态，后续的卖盘很可能出现。跌到第6根K线之前那根K线的下跌通道，很可能是一段交易区间的起点。第9根K线是在更高的低点之后两根K线多头急速行情中的第一根；这段急速行情一旦完成，多数始终入场方向的交易者都会得出结论：市场此时已经始终做多。


> When barbwire develops at the open, it is usually followed by tradable swings in both directions at some point in the day. By the third bar of the day, barbwire was likely because about half of its range was overlapped by the prior bar and it closed in its middle, meaning that the following bar would also likely overlap about half of its range. The barbwire continued right through the entire weak rally to bar 2. It was followed by a break of the bear trend line, a lower high, and then a second entry to the lower high at bar 4, which formed a double top with bar 3. The breakout to the downside over the next several bars made a trending trading range likely, especially since the range to that point was only slightly more than half of that of recent days and was likely to increase in a channel down after the spike. Traders were looking for a downside breakout and then a measured move down for their swing shorts. The downside breakout made the market always-in short, and follow-through selling was likely. The channel down to the bar before bar 6 was likely the start of a trading range. Bar 9 was the first of a two-bar bull spike after the higher low, and once that spike completed, most always-in traders would have concluded that the market was then always-in up.


涨到第7根K线的那波上涨突破了多头趋势线，随后是一个更低的低点，以及第8根K线处的两根K线反转入场做多，接着是从第9根K线更高的低点展开、一直涨到收盘的上涨行情。


> The rally to bar 7 broke the bull trend line and was followed by a lower low and a two-bar reversal buy entry at bar 8, and then the bar 9 higher low rally into the close.


第1根K线处的连续两根多头趋势K线，已足以让一些做多的剥头皮交易者在第1根K线的低点挂买入限价单，并把保护性止损放在它前面那根多头K线下方。他们在随后出现的那根空头K线上做多成交，本可以在接下来几根K线里以一到两个点的利润剥头皮出场。


> The two consecutive bull trend bars at bar 1 were enough for some bull scalpers to place buy limit orders at the low of bar 1 and protective stops below the bull bar before it. They got long on the bear bar that followed and could have scalped out with one or two points of profit over the next couple of bars.


# 第 15 章　始终入场

*15. Always In*


这也许是交易中最重要的一条概念。交易者应该不断判断市场是否处在趋势中，而“始终入场”的思路能帮交易者做出这个重要判断。如果你必须时刻留在市场里，不是做多就是做空，那么你的始终入场方向就是你当前持有的仓位方向。许多交易者——包括机构——都在用这个思路的各种变体。比如，大多数共同基金通常都是始终做多，大多数对冲基金也基本保持满仓，但它们常常在某些市场里持有始终做多的仓位，同时在另一些市场里持有始终做空的仓位。个人交易者如果往往错过太多大行情，就应该考虑采用始终入场的方法。


> This might be the single most important concept in trading. Traders should constantly assess whether the market is trending, and an “always-in” approach can help a trader to make that important determination. If you had to be in the market at all times, either long or short, the always-in position is whatever your current position is. Some variation of this is used by many traders, including institutions.
