> Bar 15 was three pushes up and the first moving average gap bar. The two-bar bull spike from bar 13 was the spike up. Spike and wedge patterns usually have two more pushes up before a correction down, as this one did.


第16根K线是一个 ii 形态，用于更高的低点做多，因为交易者预期从趋势通道过靶、以及从第13根K线低点入场那次反转之后，至少会有两段上涨。它与第14根K线那个楔形通道底部构成双底牛旗，而那条通道一直延伸到第15根K线。那根大号空头趋势K线把空头套进了空单，也把弱多头挡在了多单之外。


> Bar 16 was an ii setup for a higher low long, since traders were expecting at least two legs up from the trend channel overshoot and reversal off the bar 13 low entry. It formed a double bottom bull flag with the bar 14 bottom of the wedge channel up to bar 15. The large bear trend bar trapped bears into shorts and trapped weak bulls out of longs.


![图 21.3](figures/fig-21-03.jpg)


**图 21.3　大豆在开盘时的买入高潮**


如图 21.3 所示，大豆的5分钟图在开盘时出现一次买入高潮，随后是一个小的最终旗形，之后又出现一个楔形熊旗和一段大的第二段下跌。


> As shown in Figure 21.3, the 5 minute chart of soybeans had a buy climax on the open and then a small final flag, and later a wedge bear flag and a large second leg down.


第2根K线是第1根K线急速上涨之后的一个十字星交易区间，因此是一个糟糕的买入建仓形态。当时出现更多横盘到下跌价格行为的风险太大。激进的交易者在前一根K线的高点挂限价单做空，在第3根K线成交，他们预期这个高1会失败。第3根K线是一次低2做空、一个更低的高点，也是一个最终旗形做空。在第1根K线的买入高潮之后，交易者在寻找更大的修正，以及一次可能的开盘反转和当天的高点。


> Bar 2 was a doji trading range after the bar 1 spike up and therefore a bad buy setup. There was too much risk of more sideways to down price action. Aggressive traders placed limit orders to short at the high of the prior bar and were filled on bar 3, expecting the high 1 to fail. Bar 3 was a low 2 short, a lower high, and a final flag short. Traders were looking for more of a correction after the bar 1 buy climax and a possible opening reversal and high of the day.


第4根K线过靶了一条空头趋势通道线，并从与当天第一根K线构成的双底处反转向上。这可能是当天的最低点。入场点在第6根K线那个 ii K线上方，那根K线收成多头，且收盘价在移动平均线上方。


> Bar 4 overshot a bear trend channel line and reversed up from a double bottom with the first bar of the day. This could have been the low of the day. The entry was above the bar 6 ii bar, which had a bull close and a close above the moving average.


第9根K线是一个更低的高点楔形熊旗，并与第3根K线构成双顶熊旗。从第4根K线的低点起，它是一段四段式上涨，因此它是一个低4的变体。市场可能正在形成一段自第1根K线起的大号两段式下跌，交易者本会在第9根K线下方或者它后面那根空头K线下方做空。你可以看到，它后面那根K线是一根大号空头趋势K线，这说明许多交易者在第9根K线之后的那根空头K线下方做了空。


> Bar 9 was a lower high wedge bear flag and a double top bear flag with bar 3. It was a four-legged move up from the bar 4 low, making it a low 4 variation. The market could have been forming a large two-legged move down from bar 1, and traders would have shorted below bar 9 or below the bear bar after it. You can see how the bar after that was a large bear trend bar, indicating that many traders shorted below the bear bar after bar 9.


第10根K线是趋势线突破之后的突破回调。第11根K线是当天创出新低之后的一根大号多头反转K线，也是一个两根K线反转。然而，第12根K线没能涨到它上方。这让第12根K线成为一个很好的做空信号K线，因为在第11根K线早期入场的那些被套多头，会在第12根K线那根空头趋势K线下方出场。它同时也是一个突破回调做空的建仓形态。第13根K线是突破回调做空的入场。


> Bar 10 was a breakout pullback from the trend line breakout. Bar 11 was a huge bull reversal bar following a new low on the day and was a two-bar reversal. However, bar 12 could not trade above it. This made bar 12 a great short signal bar because the trapped longs who entered early in bar 11 would have exited below the bar 12 bear trend bar. It was also a breakout pullback short setup. Bar 13 was a breakout pullback short entry.


![图 21.4](figures/fig-21-04.jpg)


**图 21.4　原油的楔形顶部**


如图 21.4 所示，原油的5分钟图出现一个楔形顶部，随后是一个更低的高点。第1根K线是较早那个交易区间突破之后的高1突破回调。它是一个两根K线反转，也是两根K线强劲多头急速行情之后的第一次回调，这段急速行情突破了交易区间，把市场翻成了始终做多。


> As shown in Figure 21.4, the 5 minute chart of crude oil had a wedge top and then a lower high. Bar 1 was a high 1 breakout pullback from the breakout of the earlier trading range. It was a two-bar reversal and the first pullback after a strong two-bar bull spike, which broke out of a trading range and turned the market into always-in long.


第3根K线是在那根多头趋势K线上方的一次很好的高2做多，尽管有铁丝网和第二次买入高潮，因为第2根K线的顶部还不够强，不足以说明空头已经掌控了市场。


> Bar 3 was a good high 2 long above the bull trend bar, despite the barbwire and the second buy climax, because the top at bar 2 was not strong enough to indicate that the bears were in control.


第5根K线是一个楔形顶部，也是第2根K线多头急速行情之后那条通道的顶部。自第2根K线以来的双向交易还在继续，表现为醒目的影线、相互重叠的K线、回调以及空头实体，所以市场测试第3根K线那条通道低点的胜算很大。


> Bar 5 was a wedge top and the top of the channel that followed the bar 2 bull spike. The two-sided trading since bar 2 continued with prominent tails, overlapping bars, pullbacks, and bear bodies, so the odds of a test of the bar 3 channel low were good.


跌到第6根K线的这波下跌突破了趋势线，还小幅跌破了多头趋势中第3根K线那个更高的低点，说明空头很强。


> The move down to bar 6 broke the trend line and broke slightly below the bar 3 higher low of the bull trend, indicating strong bears.


第7根K线是对第 5 根信号K线低点的两段式突破回测，是跌破多头趋势线之后出现的一个更低的高点，因此可能是一次主要趋势反转，也是一个两根K线反转的做空建仓形态，还是对价格上探移动平均线之上的一次尖锐拒绝，同时是一个楔形熊旗。这个楔形熊旗的更低的高点里，第一次向上推进是第6根K线之前四根形成的那根小多头K线，第二次向上推进是第6根K线之后的那根K线。


> Bar 7 was a two-legged breakout test of the bar 5 signal bar low, a lower high after a break below the bull trend line and therefore a possible major trend reversal, a two-bar reversal short setup, a sharp rejection of the poke above the moving average, and a wedge bear flag. The first push up in the wedge bear flag lower high was the small bull bar that formed four bars before bar 6, and the second push up was the bar after bar 6.


![图 21.5](figures/fig-21-05.jpg)


**图 21.5　1分钟图上的剥头皮**


图 21.5 是一张1分钟图，显示了前 90 分钟里许多价格行为的剥头皮机会。下一张图是这一区域的放大图。对大多数交易者来说，几乎不可能足够快地正确读懂一张走势图、从而抓住其中大多数交易，但这张图说明，哪怕在1分钟这个级别上，价格行为分析也同样有效。


> Figure 21.5 is a 1 minute chart showing many price action scalps in the first 90 minutes. The next chart is a close-up of this area. It is virtually impossible for most traders to read a chart correctly fast enough to catch most of these trades, but the chart illustrates that price action analysis works even on the 1 minute level.

图 21.6 是 Emini 小型合约1分钟图前 90 分钟的放大图，突出了价格行为的剥头皮建仓形态。图中的编号与上一张图完全相同。

第1根K线是一个高2做多（此前有两次向下推进）。第2根K线是楔形做空，也是一个最终旗形。第3根K线是空头急速行情之后的一次突破回调做空和一个低1。第4根K线是突破回测做空、一个更低的高点，以及一个低2（其中第3根K线是低1）。


> Bar 1 was a high 2 long (there were two pushes down). Bar 2 was a wedge short and a final flag. Bar 3 was a breakout pullback short and a low 1 after a bear spike. Bar 4 was a breakout test short, a lower high, and a low 2 where bar 3 was the low 1.


第5根K线是一个更低的高点，也是移动平均线下方的一次低2做空。第6根K线是楔形做多、一个两根K线反转，以及一个扩张三角形底部。


> Bar 5 was a lower high and a low 2 short below the moving average. Bar 6 was a wedge long, a two-bar reversal, and an expanding triangle bottom.


第7根K线是失败的趋势线突破做空，并与第5根K线构成双顶熊旗。


> Bar 7 was a failed trend line breakout short and a double top bear flag with bar 5.


第8根K线是第7根K线突破趋势线之后的两段式更低的低点，也是交易区间日里的一个更低的低点。


> Bar 8 was a two-legged lower low after the bar 7 break of a trend line, and a lower low on a trading range day.


第10根K线是楔形反转的二次入场，也是一个更高的低点。这个更高的低点可能意味着一个多头趋势正在形成。


> Bar 10 was a wedge reversal second entry and a higher low. The higher low might have meant that a bull trend was forming.


第11根K线是趋势线突破之后的第一次回调。它是一个高2做多，其中高1出现在三根K线之前。


> Bar 11 was the first pullback after a trend line break. It was a high 2 long where the high 1 was three bars earlier.


第12根K线是又一个多头高2。第13根K线是楔形做空、一个最终旗形，以及一个可能的双顶熊旗（与第4根K线构成）。


> Bar 12 was another bull high 2. Bar 13 was a wedge short, a final flag, and a possible double top bear flag (with bar 4).


第14根K线是失败的多头趋势线突破、一次跌破交易区间的失败、一个双底牛旗，以及第二段上涨的一个可能起点。


> Bar 14 was a failed bull trend line break, a failed break below the trading range, a double bottom bull flag, and a possible start of a second leg up.


第15根K线是一个高2。两根K线之前有一个牛旗突破回调的入场。


> Bar 15 was a high 2. There was a bull flag breakout pullback entry two bars earlier.


第16根K线是多头趋势里的一个高2。第17根K线是一个楔形，也是对当天高点的一次失败测试（一个双顶），因此可能形成一个更低的高点。


> Bar 16 was a high 2 in a bull trend. Bar 17 was a wedge and a failed test of the high of the day (a double top), and therefore a possible lower high.


第19根K线是移动平均线处的一次空头低2、一个楔形熊旗，对买入第18根K线的交易者而言是一次之差五个最小报价单位的失败，也是空头急速行情把它翻成始终做空之后的一次首次回调。


> Bar 19 was a bear low 2 at the moving average, a wedge bear flag, a five-tick failure for traders who bought bar 18, and the first pullback after a bear spike that flipped the market to always-in short.


第20根K线是在一个交易区间日里两次推进、创出当天新低（第18根K线是第一次）（尽管从第17根K线的高点起有一段强劲的空头行情段，到这一步当天还不算空头日）。它同时还是在当天新低只低一个最小报价单位之后的反转向上（一次只差一个最小报价单位的突破失败和一个双底）。它也是一个楔形，以及一次两根K线最终旗形突破之后的两根K线反转向上。


> Bar 20 was two pushes to a new low of the day (bar 18 was the first) in a trading range day (even though there was a strong bear leg from the bar 17 high, it was not a bear day at this point). It was also a reversal up after a one-tick new low of the day (a one-tick failed breakout and a double bottom). It was also a wedge and a two-bar reversal up after a breakout of a two-bar final flag.


第21根K线是第二段上涨，是一个楔形熊旗（第20根K线之前的那个 ii 形态是第一次向上推进），也是一个可能的双顶熊旗（与第19根K线构成）。第22根K线是趋势线突破（第 17 到第19根K线）之后回撤到一个更高的低点的两段式回调，也是一次双底（第 10 和第20根K线）回调做多。


> Bar 21 was a second leg up, a wedge bear flag (the ii pattern before bar 20 was the first push up), and a possible double top bear flag (with bar 19). Bar 22 was a two-legged pullback to a higher low after a trend line break (bars 17 to 19) and a double bottom (bars 10 and 20) pullback long.


第23根K线是一次失败的趋势线突破，也是一个双底（第23根K线比第22根K线高一个最小报价单位）牛旗。


> Bar 23 was a failed trend line break and a double bottom (bar 23 was one tick higher than bar 22) bull flag.


# 第 22 章　日线图、周线图与月线图

*22. Daily, Weekly, and Monthly Charts*


日线图、周线图和月线图虽然都可能给出日内信号，但这类信号出现得太少，对日内交易者来说反而成了一种干扰，应当忽略。最常见的信号是基于昨日高点和低点的那类信号，而你在5分钟图上就能看到它们。不过，这些更长的时间级别上也常常有价格行为的入场机会；只是信号K线太大，如果风险要和一笔日内交易一样，能够交易的合约数就少得多。此外，隔夜风险可能意味着你应当把合约数再减少一些，或者考虑去做风险有限的期权策略，比如直接买入期权或价差组合。日内交易者只有在这些图不会在交易时间里占据自己思绪的前提下，才该去交易它们，因为一面照看一笔基于日线图、合约数或股数少得多的交易，一面很容易错过几笔用大成交量做的日内交易，而这些错过的交易，可能把日线信号带来的收益抵消掉还有余。


> Although daily, weekly, and monthly charts can generate intraday signals, they occur so infrequently that they become a distraction for a day trader and should be ignored. The most common signals are those based on yesterday's high and low, and you can see them on a 5 minute chart. However, there are frequently price action entries on these longer time frames, but because the signal bars are so large, far fewer contracts can be traded if the risk is to be the same as for a day trade. Also, overnight risk may mean that you should reduce your contracts even further or consider trading option strategies that have a limited risk, like outright purchases or spreads. A day trader should trade these charts only if they do not occupy his thoughts during the trading day, because it is easy to miss a few day trades using large volume while nursing a trade of far fewer contracts or shares based on the daily chart, and these misses can more than offset any gain from the daily signal.


所有股票都会形成标准的价格行为形态，但机构持股很少的微型公司股票，出现异常大涨大跌的风险很大。这类股票往往波动性更高，在股市术语里被称为高贝塔股票（high-beta stocks）。举例来说，你不会指望沃尔玛（WMT）在一个月里涨 1,000%，可当一家小型制药公司唯一的那款药获得美国食品药品监督管理局（FDA）的批准，或者它突然成为收购标的时，这种情况恰恰可能发生。有些交易者喜欢这种巨大、快速的行情，但大多数交易者宁愿避开风险：一是价格可能突然朝两个方向大幅波动，二是自己的交易可能成交得很差。做这类特殊情况的交易者必须非常密切地盯盘，这就让他们很难同时交易别的股票。由于风险太大，他们只能拿投资组合的一小部分这样交易，而这抹掉了从那些大涨大跌中得来的大部分收益。再加上不可预测带来的压力，大多数交易者都不该去碰这些股票。


> Although all stocks form standard price action patterns, stocks of very small companies that have little institutional ownership have a significant risk of unusually big moves up and down. They tend to be more volatile, and in stock market terminology, these stocks are called high-beta stocks. For example, you would not expect Wal-Mart (WMT) to jump 1,000 percent in a month, but when a small drug company gets its one drug approved by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) or is suddenly a takeover candidate, this is exactly what can happen. Some traders like the huge, fast moves, but most traders prefer to avoid the risk of sudden, huge moves in both directions and bad fills on their trades. Traders who trade these special situations have to watch the stocks very closely, which makes it difficult for them to trade other stocks at the same time. Since the risk is so great, they can only trade a small portion of their portfolio this way and this erases most of the gain derived from the big moves. When you add the stress of the unpredictability, most traders should not bother with these stocks.


逆着强趋势交易时，目标应当是赚 1% 或 2% 的剥头皮，因为大多数逆势交易的结果只是变成回调，而这些回调随后又变成顺势入场的机会。跳空会让入场变得复杂；总的来说，如果市场开在昨日区间之内，随后穿过挂在区间外一个最小报价单位处的入场止损单，风险会小一些。如果你没法盯盘中走势，而当天又是跳空开盘，那多半最好放弃这笔交易。如果你能盯盘，而当天跳空开盘，那就等一次跳空回调，然后在这波回落进入缺口失败、市场重新朝远离昨日区间的方向走时入场。换句话说，如果你本来想买入，但今天向上跳空，那就找开盘后的一波抛售，然后在它反转向上的开盘反转时买入，把保护性止损放在今日低点下方。如果这笔入场失败、止损被打掉，就去看别的股票；只有在出现第二个买入建仓形态时，才再给它一次机会。别在一只不按你想法走的股票上花太多时间，因为你会亏钱。亏钱之后想从同一只股票上把钱赚回来，是一种很自然的倾向，但这是你情绪脆弱的表现。如果你觉得非要证明自己判断正确、确实是个了不起的看图高手，那你也许确实看得对，但你并不是个了不起的交易者。了不起的交易者接受亏损，然后继续往前走。


> When trading counter to a strong trend, the goal should be a scalp of 1 or 2 percent, since most countertrend trades just result in pullbacks that become with-trend entries. Gaps complicate the entries and, in general, the risk is less if the market opens within yesterday's range and then trades through the entry stop at one tick beyond that range. If you cannot watch the stock intraday and there is a gap open, it is probably best to pass on the trade. If you can watch the stock and there is a gap opening, watch for a gap pullback and then enter on the failed pullback into the gap, as the market resumes its move away from yesterday's range. In other words, if you were looking to buy but today gapped up, look for a sell-off on the open today and then buy an opening reversal back up, placing your protective stop below the low of today. If the entry fails and your stop is hit, look elsewhere or give it only one more try if there is a second buy setup. Don't spend too much time on a stock that is not doing what you wanted it to do, because you will lose money. There is a natural tendency to want to make back your money on the same stock after a loss, but this is a sign of your emotional weakness. If you feel a need to prove that you were right and are in fact a great chart reader, you might be right about that, but you are not a great trader. Great traders accept their losses and move on.


日线图上的回调很少出现经典的反转K线，这让交易者比交易5分钟图时面临更多的不确定性。不确定性意味着风险，而风险更大时，仓位规模就要更小，交易者还必须考虑先建一部分仓位，随着价格行为展开再加仓。在多头回调里，如果市场再跌一点、但空头还没有表现出掌控了局面，就可以在更低的价格加仓。也可以在趋势恢复、一次小回调在你的原始入场价上方形成更高的低点之后，在更高的价格加仓。


> Pullbacks on daily charts rarely have classic reversal bars, leaving traders with more uncertainty than when trading 5 minute charts. Uncertainty means risk, and when there is more risk, position sizes need to be smaller, and a trader will have to consider taking a partial position and adding to the position as the price action unfolds. In a bull pullback, additions can be made at a lower price if the market sells off a little more, but the bears have not yet demonstrated that they are in control. Additions can also be made at a higher price after the trend has resumed and a small pullback forms a higher low above your original entry.


收盘后扫一遍日线图，你常常会看到一些值得第二天考虑的建仓形态。建仓形态一旦触发，往往会出现一段日内趋势，给你提供许多不错的5分钟顺势入场机会。如果这只股票不是你平时做日内交易的品种，但成交量大约在 500 万股以上，那就值得考虑把它加进你的日内交易股票池，做上一两天。不过有时候，即便是像石油服务 HOLDRS（OIH）这样流动性很好的股票，你的经纪商也可能没有可供卖空的券源，你也许只能做买入类的建仓形态。如果你确实想做空，可以改为买入看跌期权，即便是做日内交易也行。


> When you scan your daily charts at the end of the day, you will frequently see setups to consider for the next day. Once the setup triggers, there will often be an intraday trend that will provide you with many good 5 minute with-trend entries. If the stock is not one that you normally trade intraday but its volume is about five million shares or more, it is worth considering adding it to your basket of day trading stocks for a day or two. Sometimes, however, even with very liquid stocks such as the Oil Service HOLDRS (OIH), your broker might not have an inventory available for selling short, and you might only be able to trade buy setups. If you really want to short, you can buy puts instead, even for a day trade.


整数关口（round numbers）是磁力位，因此它们能够形成交易机会。举例来说，如果自由港麦克莫兰（FCX）在过去几个月里涨了 20%，现在成交在 93，许多交易者就会假定它会到 100。正因如此，空头不会大力做空，因为他们相信自己很快就能在更好的价位做空；多头会大力买入，因为他们相信 FCX 会涨到那个磁力位之上。空头的缺席制造出一种真空效应，常常让这只股票迅速涨到磁力位。它通常会先涨到磁力位上方 5% 到 10%，然后才回调；而在决定下一步怎么做之前，它通常至少会回调到整数关口下方一次。多头可以在它上涨进入整数关口的磁场时买入，就在其上方止盈；空头可以等到市场涨到上方之后再去做空，然后在回测向下时止盈。多头通常会在那里再次买入，做一次剥头皮。


> Since round numbers are magnets, they can set up trades. For example, if Freeport-McMoRan (FCX) is up 20 percent over the past few months and is now trading at 93, many traders will assume that it will reach 100. Because of this, bears will not short aggressively, because they believe that they soon will be able to short at a better price, and bulls will buy aggressively because they believe that FCX will go above the magnet. This absence of bears creates a vacuum effect that often results in the stock quickly moving up to the magnet. It will typically go 5 to 10 percent above the magnet before it pulls back, and it usually pulls back below the round number at least once before it decides what it will do next. Bulls can buy as it rallies into the magnetic field of the round number and take profits just above it, and bears can wait to short until the market is above and then take profits on the test back down. Bulls will usually buy again there for a scalp.


![图 22.1](figures/fig-22-01.jpg)


**图 22.1　价格行为从未改变**


价格行为是大量交易者各自出于数不清的理由、为尽可能多赚钱而独立行动所累积起来的结果。正因如此，它的指纹始终没有改变，对读得懂它的人来说，它将永远是一个可靠的赚钱工具。图 22.1 是 1932 年和 1933 年道琼斯工业平均指数的日线图，它看上去和今天任何时间级别上交易着的任何一只股票没什么两样。


> Price action is the cumulative result of a large number of traders acting independently for countless reasons to make as much money as they can. Because of that, its fingerprint has remained unchanged and will always provide a reliable tool for making money for those who can read it. Figure 22.1 is a daily chart of the Dow Jones Industrial Average in 1932 and 1933, and it looks like any stock trading today on any time frame.


第2根K线是一个低2，突破了趋势线。


> Bar 2 was a low 2 that broke a trend line.


第3根K线是一次小的最终旗形反转，也是趋势线突破之后对第1根K线低点的更低的低点测试（一次趋势线突破之后再出现一次测试，可能构成主要趋势反转）。


> Bar 3 was a small final flag reversal and a lower low test of the bar 1 low after a trend line break (a trend line break and then a test can be a major trend reversal).


第4根K线是一次突破回调，也是一个小的更高的低点。第5根K线是强大多头急速行情中的第一次回调，是一个高2。第6根K线是多头急速行情之后的楔形通道，它引出了两段大幅下跌，止于第8根K线。


> Bar 4 was a breakout pullback and a small higher low. Bar 5 was the first pullback in a strong bull spike and a high 2. Bar 6 was a wedge channel after the bull spike and led to two large legs down, ending at bar 8.


第7根K线是一次趋势线突破，也是一次两段式回调。它是一面大型楔形牛旗的突破，那面旗形的第一次下推出现在第5根K线。


> Bar 7 was a trend line break and a two-legged pullback. It was the breakout of a large wedge bull flag that had its first push down at bar 5.


第8根K线是一次更低的低点主要趋势反转，也是一次突破回调、一面更大的楔形牛旗，以及对第2根K线的突破回测。


> Bar 8 was a lower low major trend reversal and breakout pullback, a larger wedge bull flag, and a breakout test of bar 2.


第10根K线是一个更高的低点，也是第9根K线突破第7根K线到第8根K线的空头通道之后的回调。空头通道就是牛旗。


> Bar 10 was a higher low and a pullback from the bar 9 breakout above the bear channel from bar 7 to bar 8. A bear channel is a bull flag.


第11根K线是一次小的高2突破回调，发生在市场突破那面已经失败的第7根和第9根K线双顶熊旗之后。


> Bar 11 was a small high 2 breakout pullback after the breakout above the failed bars 7 and 9 double top bear flag.


第12根和第13根K线都是小级别趋势线突破之后反转向上的走势。第14根K线是一个楔形，也是一次小的最终旗形反转。第15根K线是一波强动能的逆势行情，在上涨行情测试第14根K线高点之后，它很可能会被测试。它与第13根K线构成双底牛旗，但它向下的力度足够强，市场可能已经翻成始终做空。交易者会去找更高的高点来做空，如果做多会让他们在更高的高点做空变得更难，他们就不会在这里买入。有时候，交易者一面在做多剥头皮，一面又在找更高的高点做空，等做空形态真的形成时，他们就没法把心态切换过来去做空。


> Bars 12 and 13 were reversals up after minor trend line breaks. Bar 14 was a wedge and a small final flag reversal. Bar 15 was a strong-momentum countertrend move that would likely be tested after a rally tested the bar 14 high. It formed a double bottom bull flag with bar 13, but it was strong enough down so that the market might have flipped to always-in short. Traders would have looked to short a lower high and would not have looked to buy here if the long would have made it more difficult for them to get short on the lower high. Sometimes when traders scalp a long when they are looking to short a lower high, they cannot change their mind-set to short as the short is setting up.


第16根K线是一个楔形的更低的高点，第17根K线是该楔形的一次突破失败。


> Bar 16 was a wedge lower high, and bar 17 was a failed breakout of the wedge.


第18根K线是对第14根K线多头趋势极值的更低的高点测试，也是楔形更高的高点突破回调中的一次低2做空入场。楔形下方曾出现一次突破失败，而涨到第18根K线的这波上涨，是从该楔形出发的更高的高点突破回调。另一些交易者则认为，它只是一个比止于第16根K线的那一个更好的楔形。第18根K线也是对第14根K线信号K线低点的突破回测。


> Bar 18 was the lower high test of the bar 14 bull trend extreme and was a low 2 entry for a short on the wedge higher high breakout pullback. There was a failed breakout below the wedge, and the rally to bar 18 was a higher high breakout pullback from the wedge. Other traders saw it as simply a better wedge than the one that ended at bar 16. Bar 18 was also a breakout test of the bar 14 signal bar low.


第19根K线是对第15根K线低点的测试，是一个双底牛旗。第20根K线是反转上涨过程中的一次更高的低点回调。


> Bar 19 was the test of the bar 15 low and was a double bottom bull flag. Bar 20 was a higher low pullback in the reversal up.


![图 22.2](figures/fig-22-02.jpg)


**图 22.2　跳空回调**


如图 22.2 所示，当日线图上出现买入建仓形态、而市场向上跳空到昨日高点上方时，交易者往往会等5分钟图上回调后再买入。AAPL 在日线图（缩略图）上处于强多头趋势中，并在第1根K线处出现第一次均线回调，那是一次空头趋势通道的过靶（两张图上的编号相同）。日线图上第2根K线在盘中强劲反转向上，收盘接近它的高点。在日线图第2根K线高点上方一个最小报价单位处买入是合理的，那个高点就是5分钟图上第3根K线的高点。然而，第二天的开盘跳空到第2日高点上方。与其去冒可能出现反转下跌日的风险，更谨慎的做法是在5分钟图上等待市场回调测试缺口之后的那个反转向上。


> As shown in Figure 22.2, when there is a buy setup on the daily chart and the market gaps above yesterday's high, traders will often wait to buy a pullback on the 5 minute chart. AAPL was in a strong bull trend on the daily chart (thumbnail) and had a first moving average pullback at bar 1, which was a bear trend channel overshoot (the numbering is the same on both charts). Bar 2 on the daily chart had a strong intraday reversal up and closed near its high. It was reasonable to want to buy at one tick above the high of bar 2 on the daily chart, which was the high of bar 3 on the 5 minute chart. However, the next day gapped above the day 2 high. Rather than risk a possible reversal down day, it would have been prudent to watch for a reversal up after a pullback test of the gap on the 5 minute chart.


5分钟图上第6根K线回补了缺口，它是一根均线缺口K线，也是一次空头趋势通道的过靶和反转向上。这是一次很好的做多入场，保护性止损放在第6根K线下方。这 62 美分的风险带来了几美元的收益。


> Bar 6 on the 5 minute chart closed the gap and was a moving average gap bar and a bear trend channel overshoot and reversal up. This was a great long entry with a protective stop below bar 6. This 62 cent risk led to a several-dollar gain.


![图 22.3](figures/fig-22-03.jpg)


**图 22.3　SPY 的周线图**


如图 22.3 所示，SPY 的周线图看起来像是处于一波熊市反弹之中，因为从第16根K线到第32根K线的这波上涨，斜率比跌到第16根K线的那波抛售更平缓。此外，市场没能守在由上方交易区间底部的第6、第8和第10根K线低点所形成的阻力之上。不过，这波上涨已经回撤了跌到第16根K线的空头趋势的很大一部分，空头趋势剩下的影响力已经不多，市场因此变成了一个大型交易区间。如果它是一波熊市反弹，那么它最终就应该测试第16根K线低点。多头希望市场继续上行，突破自第3根K线开始的空头趋势中的那些摆动高点，最终向上突破、创出历史新高。空头希望市场在第21、22、23、27 和 32 根K线构成的扩张三角形中失败，然后跌破三角形第27根K线的底部，随后创出低于第16根K线的新的空头低点。由于这波上涨如此之大，这张图已经更像一个大型交易区间，并且失去了趋势所带来的那种确定性。不确定性是交易区间的标志；一旦市场显得不确定，它通常就处在交易区间之中，这里的情况正是如此。


> As shown in Figure 22.3, the weekly chart of the SPY looks like it is in a bear rally because the move up from bar 16 to bar 32 has a shallower slope than the sell-off down to bar 16. Also, the market is not holding above the resistance created by the lows of bars 6, 8, and 10 at the bottom of the upper trading range. However, the rally has retraced so much of the bear trend down to bar 16 that the bear trend does not have much influence left, and the market has therefore become a large trading range. If it is a bear rally, then it should eventually test the bar 16 low. The bulls want the market to continue to go above the swing highs in the bear trend down from bar 3 and eventually to break out to a new all-time high. The bears want the market to fail in an expanding triangle formed by bars 21, 22, 23, 27, and 32, and then break below the bar 27 bottom of the triangle and subsequently to a new bear low below bar 16. Since the rally has been so big, the chart has become more of a large trading range and it has lost the certainty that comes from a trend. Uncertainty is the hallmark of a trading range; once a market appears uncertain, it is usually in a trading range, as is the case here.


在从第3根K线开始的下跌中，市场开始在第5、第9和第11根K线形成更低的高点，在第6、第8、第10和第12根K线形成更低的低点。由于当时还没有出现强劲的空头突破，概率上更支持这波抛售是对交易区间底部的测试，或者是一面可能的大型牛旗。有些交易者认为，跌到第6根K线的空头急速行情也许已经把市场变成始终做空，但对那些仍有怀疑的交易者来说，跌到第13根K线的空头急速行情才把始终入场方向翻成了做空。


> On the move down from bar 3, the market began forming lower highs at bars 5, 9, and 11 and lower lows at bars 6, 8, 10, and 12. Since there was yet to be a strong bear breakout, the odds favored this sell-off as being a test of the bottom of the trading range or a possible large bull flag. Some traders believed that the bear spike down to bar 6 might have turned the market to always-in short, but the bear spike down to bar 13 flipped the always-in position to short for any traders who were still in doubt.


第14根K线是第二次卖出高潮的第三根K线，也是一次最终旗形之后尝试形成的两根K线反转，但市场又一次下跌，走出从第15根K线开始的急速行情与高潮式空头下跌。这是第三次卖出高潮，也是一个楔形底（第13、14 和 16 根K线）。底部刚过基于上方交易区间高度算出的等距运动目标位。


> Bar 14 was the third bar of a second sell climax and an attempt at a two-bar reversal from a final flag, but the market fell once again in a spike and climax bear down from bar 15. This was the third sell climax and a wedge bottom (bars 13, 14, and 16). The bottom was just past the measured move target based on the height of the upper trading range.


涨到第17根K线的这波上涨有12根多头实体、影线很小，而且只有少数几根多头实体，其强度足以被大多数交易者看成一段急速行情。在第16根K线低点处的三次卖出高潮和这波向上急速行情之后，交易者认为，至少应该还有第二段上涨，甚至可能基于第16根K线低点以及第15根K线顶部或第17根K线高点，走出一段向上的等距运动。第23根K线略高于等距运动目标位和趋势通道线顶部，并在上方交易区间底部第6、第8和第10根K线所在的区域，形成一次向下的两根K线反转。第一个目标是跌破通道，这一点在第24根K线实现。第二段下跌止于第27根K线的两根K线反转。第29根K线在第28根K线突破从第23根K线开始的两段式牛旗之后，形成了一次更高的低点突破回调。它同时还是一个头肩形态底部牛旗的右肩，其左肩形成于第24根K线和第25根K线之间。第21根K线到第28根K线之间的这个交易区间，也是一个头肩形态的顶部，其中第21根K线是左肩，第23根K线是头，第26根K线和第28根K线构成的双顶是右肩。就像 80% 的顶部形态那样，市场向上突破，空头再一次学到：大多数顶部不过是牛旗。


> The move up to bar 17 had 12 bull bodies, small tails, and only a couple of bull bodies and was strong enough to be considered a spike by most traders. After the three sell climaxes at the bar 16 low and this spike up, traders thought that there should be at least a second leg up and possibly a measured move up based on the bar 16 low and the top of the bar 15 or bar 17 high. Bar 23 was just slightly above the measured move target and the top of the trend channel line, and it was a two-bar reversal down in the area of the bars 6, 8, and 10 bottom of the upper trading range. The first target was a break below the channel, which occurred at bar 24. A second leg down ended at the bar 27 two-bar reversal. Bar 29 formed a higher low breakout pullback after the bar 28 breakout of the two-legged bull flag down from bar 23. It was also the right shoulder of a head and shoulders bottom bull flag where the left shoulder formed between bar 24 and bar 25. The trading range between bar 21 and bar 28 was also a head and shoulders top, where bar 21 was the left shoulder, bar 23 was the head, and the bars 26 and 28 double top was the right shoulder. As happens in 80 percent of topping patterns, the market broke to the upside and the bears learned once again that most tops are just bull flags.


从第29根K线到第32根K线的走势处在一个相当紧的多头通道里，之后很容易出现更高的价格。不过，由于整张图是一个大型交易区间，大涨之后通常跟着大跌，市场可能很快就会开始向下修正，跌到扩张三角形第27根K线的底部，甚至跌到第16根K线空头低点所在的区域。


> The move from bar 29 to bar 32 was in a fairly tight bull channel and could easily be followed by higher prices. However, since the entire chart is a large trading range, big rallies are usually followed by big sell-offs, and the market might soon begin to correct down to the bar 27 bottom of the expanding triangle, or even to the area of the bar 16 bear low.


第16根K线是一段向下的等距运动。大多数机构只做他们相信会成立的交易，也就是说概率至少有 60%。因此，他们至少需要一段等距运动，交易者等式才能为正（等距运动的位置，正是回报变得和风险一样大、交易者等式开始变得比较有利可图的地方）。结果是，交易常常会精确地打到一个目标位，然后反转，或者至少停顿下来，因为许多机构会在那里止盈部分或全部仓位。大多数目标位，就像所有的支撑和阻力一样，很快会失败，因为等距运动只是最低要求，而许多机构会觉得市场强得足以走得更远。


> Bar 16 was a measured move down. Most institutions take trades that they believe will work, which means that the probability is at least 60 percent. They therefore need at least a measured move to have a positive trader's equation (the measured move is where the reward becomes as large as the risk, and the trader's equation begins to become reasonably profitable). The result is that trades often hit a target exactly and then reverse or at least pause, because many firms will take partial or full profits there. Most targets, like all support and resistance, soon fail, because the measured move is the minimum needed, and many firms will feel that the market is strong enough to go well beyond.

**图 22.4　黄金月线图的楔形通道**


如图 22.4 所示，黄金月线图在第7根K线到第8根K线的多头急速行情之后，处在一个楔形通道里。有些交易者会把当前这波上涨看成第三次推进，其中第11根和第13根K线是前两次推进。另一些人则把第8根或第9根K线看作第一次推进。


> As shown in Figure 22.4, the monthly gold chart is in a wedge channel after the bull spike from bar 7 to bar 8. Some traders will see the current move as the third push up where bars 11 and 13 were the first two pushes. Others see bar 8 or 9 as the first push.


每当有 5 到 10 根K线贴着某条趋势线运行时，市场很快跌破这条趋势线的概率就很大。这就让从第10根K线开始的向上多头趋势线容易被向下突破。由于市场刚刚处在趋势通道线和等距运动目标位上方，概率上更支持很快就开始一段两段式抛售。市场至少应当向下修正到第8根K线高点下方一点，也可能修正到楔形第10根K线的底部。可能性较小的情况是：市场向上突破楔形顶部，并走出一段向上的等距运动。


> Whenever five to 10 bars are close to a trend line, the odds are good that the market will soon fall below the trend line. This makes the bull trend line up from bar 10 vulnerable to a downside breakout. Since the market is just above the trend channel line and the measured move target, the odds favor a two-legged sell-off starting very soon. At a minimum, the market should correct to just below the bar 8 high, and it might correct to the bar 10 bottom of the wedge. Less likely, there will be an upside breakout of the wedge top and a measured move up.

如图 22.5 所示，美元期货的月线图上有好几笔交易算得上是最佳交易。美元和瑞郎、日元一样，属于避险货币（risk-off currencies），交易者在认为股市会下跌时，往往就会买入它们。

美元向上急涨，突破了第2根K线处熊旗的顶部，把市场变成了始终做多。随后它形成一个通道，接着是第5根K线对通道起点第3根K线底部的测试。这在第5根K线处形成双底牛旗，之后又在第7根K线给出一个突破回调的买入建仓形态。市场在第11根K线的更高的高点处见顶。有些交易者把从第3根K线到第11根K线的走势看成一个宽通道，另一些人则认为通道从第5根或第7根K线开始。所有交易者都怀疑第11根或第13根K线可能是向下修正到通道底部的起点，因为市场正在变得双向，出现了好几次反转和几根实体醒目的空头K线。这些都代表着不断累积的卖压。


> The dollar had a bull spike up as it broke above the top of the bear flag at bar 2, converting the market to always-in long. This created a double bottom bull flag at bar 5 and was followed by a breakout pullback buy setup at bar 7. The market topped out at the bar 11 higher high. Some traders saw the move from bar 3 to bar 11 as a broad channel, and others saw the channel as starting at bars 5 or 7. All traders suspected that bar 11 or bar 13 could be the start of the correction down to the bottom of the channel, because the market was becoming two-sided with several reversals and prominent bear bodies. These represented accumulating selling pressure.


跌到第10根K线的那根K线是一根强劲的空头趋势K线，它跌破了从第7根K线开始的陡峭多头趋势线（图中未画出）。这波下跌力度足够强，让许多多头在涨到第11根K线新高的这波上涨中止盈。空头在那个更高的高点开始做空，在第13根K线的更低的高点主要趋势反转处，做空更加激进。跌到第12根K线的下跌中有两根强劲的空头趋势K线，并且跌破了多头趋势线。市场本应至少走出两段下跌，但它却先是空头急速行情跌到第14根K线，然后走出一段通道下跌，跌到第18根K线。跌到第14根K线的这波下跌让大多数交易者相信，市场已经翻成始终做空，因此后面应该有更多的卖盘。


> The move down to bar 10 was a strong bear trend bar, and it broke below a steep bull trend line up from bar 7 (not shown). This was a strong enough move to make many bulls take profits on the rally to the new high at bar 11. Bears started shorting at that higher high and even more aggressively at the bar 13 lower high major trend reversal. The move down to bar 12 had two strong bear trend bars and broke below the bull trend line. The market should have had at least two legs down, but instead it had a bear spike down to bar 14 and then a channel down to bar 18. The move down to bar 14 convinced most traders that the market had flipped to always-in short and therefore should be followed by more selling.


空头通道一路下跌到第18根K线，它是大跌空头趋势末端一次卖出高潮中的第五根K线。交易者预期会出现一波上涨行情，至少涨到均线。它同时与第1根K线构成双底。


> The bear channel continued down to bar 18, which was the fifth bar in a sell climax at the end of a big bear trend. Traders expected a rally, at least to the moving average. It was also a double bottom with bar 1.


在均线处曾出现一次“20 根均线缺口K线”的做空机会，但由于向上急速行情很强，更好的做法是等第二个信号。第二个信号出现在第19根K线那根均线缺口K线上，它与第17根K线之后那波小上涨行情的高点构成双顶熊旗。


> There was a 20 gap bar short at the moving average, but since the spike up was strong, it was better to wait for a second signal. The second signal came with the bar 19 moving average gap bar, which formed a double top bear flag with the high of the small rally after bar 17.


跌到第20根K线的急速行情之后，是一段抛物线式、因而属于高潮式的通道下跌，一直跌到第22根K线，市场在那里形成了一次更低的低点主要趋势反转。在那里，市场横盘，形成一个iii形态的变体（只看实体）。其间出现过一次失败的低1做空，随后在一个小双底处反转向上；而涨到第23根K线的多头急速行情格外强劲。这很可能把市场翻成始终做多，并会让多头设法把市场保持在急速行情底部之上。他们在低点附近大力买入，在第27根和第29根K线也这样做，形成双底牛旗。第27根K线是一次双底主要趋势反转，第29根K线是三角形中第三次下推之后反转向上的走势，这个三角形最终可能向上或向下突破。


> The spike down to bar 20 was followed by a parabolic and therefore climactic channel down to bar 22, where the market formed a lower low major trend reversal. There, the market went sideways in a variation of an iii pattern (bodies only). It had a failed low 1 short that reversed up in a small double bottom, and the bull spike up to bar 23 was exceptionally strong. This probably flipped the market to always-in long and would have made the bulls try to keep the market above the bottom of the spike. They bought aggressively near the low and they also did at bars 27 and 29, creating a double bottom bull flag. Bar 27 was a double bottom major trend reversal, and bar 29 was a reversal up from the third push down in a triangle, which could ultimately have a breakout up or down.


楔形牛旗（第24、26、27根K线）之后又是一波上涨，然后在第29根K线形成双底。对做多来说，这是一个风险回报比很好的建仓形态，因为交易者买入的位置在交易区间的底部。由于市场处于交易区间的底部，走出一段等距上涨的概率也许是 60%。风险大约 5.00 美元，而测试交易区间顶部第28根K线高点的概率是 60%。交易者冒 5.00 美元的风险去赚 10.00 美元，成功概率 60%，这非常好。每笔交易的平均盈利大约是 4.00 美元。由于这同时也是一个双底牛旗，成功率也许高于 60%。目标将是从这个交易区间向上走出一段等距运动，并测试到空头通道第15根K线顶部附近。


> The wedge bull flag (bars 24, 26, 27) was followed by another rally and then a double bottom at bar 29. This was a good risk/reward setup for a long, since a trader would be buying at the bottom of a trading range. The probability of an equidistant move up was probably 60 percent, since the market was at the bottom of a trading range. The risk was about $5.00 with a 60 percent chance of a test of the bar 28 top of the trading range. A trader would be risking $5.00 to make $10.00 with a probability of 60 percent, which is very good. The average profit per trade would be about $4.00. Since this was also a double bottom bull flag, the odds were probably better than 60 percent. The target would be a measured move up out of this trading range, and it would test to around the bar 15 top of the bear channel.


重要的是要意识到，这意味着市场约有 40% 的概率会跌破第22根K线低点，所以一旦发生，交易者就需要出场。如果真跌破，下一个目标就是一段向下的等距运动，依据是第27根K线到第28根K线、或者第22根K线到第23根K线那两段下跌的高度。


> It is important to realize that this means that there was about a 40 percent chance that the market would fall below the bar 22 low, so traders would need to exit if that happened. If it did, the next target would be a measured move down, based on the height of the bar 27 to 28 or bar 22 to 23 legs down.


即便市场确实上涨，概率上更支持它会在第11根K线高点附近停滞下来，形成一个更大的交易区间。


> Even if the market does go up, the odds favor that it will stall around the bar 11 high and form a larger trading range.


![图 22.6](figures/fig-22-06.jpg)


**图 22.6　整数关口可以是支撑和阻力**


如图 22.6 所示，这张日线图说明了处于强多头趋势中的 AAPL 如何在重要的整数关口下方停滞，而整数关口往往是吸引市场向它们靠拢的磁力位。一旦足够多的交易者相信这个磁力位会被触及，空头就停止做空，市场在上涨真空里一路涨到目标位上方。举例来说，空头相信市场会涨到 300 美元上方，而且很可能至少高出 5% 到 10%，因为市场一旦进入某个整数关口的磁力吸引范围，通常就是这样走的。由于空头预期市场会涨到 315 美元左右（比整数关口高 5%），他们就退到了一边。既然他们相信市场在几根K线之内就会更高，那么在市场涨到那里之前做空就毫无道理。他们的缺席让市场快速上涨，因为多头不得不把市场推得更高，才能找到足够多的交易者接下自己多单的另一边。


> As shown in Figure 22.6, this daily chart illustrates how AAPL, which was in a strong bull trend, stalled below significant round numbers, which are often magnets that draw the market to them. Once enough traders became convinced that the magnet would be reached, the bears stopped shorting, and the market rallied in a buy vacuum to above the target. For example, the bears believed that the market would get above $300 and probably at least 5 to 10 percent above, because that is what the market usually does once it is in the magnetic pull of a round number. Since the bears expected the market to reach around $315 (5 percent above the round number), they stepped aside. It did not make sense for them to short before the market got there when they believed that the market would be higher within a few bars. Their absence caused the market to go up quickly, since the bulls had to push the market up higher to find enough traders to take the opposite side of their longs.


一旦市场涨到目标位上方 5% 到 10%，多头就开始止盈，空头则开始做空，期待一次回到整数关口的向下测试，而那个关口通常至少会被穿破一次。跌到第12根K线低点的那次回调距离 300 美元只差一美分（第12根K线低点是 300.01 美元），随后市场在当天收盘前大幅上涨。第13根K线附近的双顶做空成功把 AAPL 打到了 300 美元下方，但买方又回来了，在第14根K线形成双底。


> Once the market gets 5 to 10 percent above the target, bulls begin to take profits and bears begin to short for a test back down to the round number, which usually gets penetrated at least once. The pullback to the bar 12 low missed $300 by a penny (the bar 12 low was $300.01) and the market rallied sharply into the close of that day. Double top shorts around bar 13 succeeded in driving AAPL below $300, but the buyers came back and formed the bar 14 double bottom.


![图 22.7](figures/fig-22-07.jpg)


**图 22.7　日线图与月线图可能处在相反的趋势中**


如图 22.7 所示，小麦在右侧的日线图上走出一波急速上涨，但在左侧的月线图上，它只是一波熊市反弹；在那里，第10根K线在空头趋势中形成一根均线缺口K线，与第7根K线构成双顶熊旗，并且是对上方交易区间（一个头肩形态的顶部）底部第3根和第5根K线的突破回测。两张图上的编号相同。


> As shown in Figure 22.7, wheat had a sharp rally on the daily chart on the right, but it was just a bear market rally on the monthly chart on the left, where bar 10 formed a moving average gap bar in the bear trend, a double top bear flag with bar 7, and a breakout test of the bars 3 and 5 bottom of the upper trading range (a head and shoulders top). The numbering is the same for both charts.


在日线图上第10根空头反转K线形成的前一天，一位电视评论员说小麦会涨得高得多，他正在市价买入，也在回调时买入。当一段趋势在一段漫长的多头急速行情（10 到 20 根K线）之后出现大的多头趋势K线时，就有很大的风险走出一段旷日持久的两段式回调，因为大多数强多头只肯买一次像样的回调，而大多数强空头会市价做空、并在更高的位置分批建仓。这位电视评论员关于小麦会涨得多的判断，最终也许是对的，但他在一段抛物线式急速行情与高潮的顶部买入，占用了太多资金。他本该去做机构当时正在做的事。那时空头在做空，多头在等一次两段式回调之后再买入。


> On the day before the bar 10 bear reversal bar formed on the daily chart, a television pundit said that wheat was going much higher and that he was buying it at the market and on pullbacks. When a trend forms large bull trend bars after a long bull spike (10 to 20 bars), there is a great risk of a protracted two-legged pullback because most strong bulls would only buy a significant pullback and most strong bears would short at the market and scale in higher. The television pundit might ultimately be right about wheat going a lot higher, but he was tying up too much of his capital by buying at the top of a parabolic spike and climax. Instead, he should have been doing what the institutions were doing. The bears were shorting and the bulls were waiting for a two-legged pullback before buying.


在第10根K线的前一天，消息面显然对小麦非常利多，但这并不重要。图告诉交易者的是：强空头和强多头都预期会出现一次大幅修正。急速行情与抛物线式高潮告诉交易者：弱多头和弱空头在做错误的事，而强多头和强空头正在对这次回调下注。交易赚钱最好的办法，就是去做聪明钱正在做的事，别去听电视上的专家。聪明钱的规模如此之大，那些聪明的交易者根本藏不住他们在做什么。不过，你必须会读图，才能看懂正在发生什么。


> On the day before bar 10, the news was obviously very bullish for wheat, but that is irrelevant. The chart told traders that strong bears and bulls were expecting a large correction. The spike and parabolic climax told traders that the weak bulls and bears were doing the wrong thing and that the strong bulls and bears were betting on the pullback. The best way to make money trading is by doing what the smart money is doing and not listening to experts on television. The smart money is so huge that those smart traders cannot hide what they are doing. However, you must be able to read the chart to understand what is going on.


![图 22.8](figures/fig-22-08.jpg)


**图 22.8　消息面可以推动一只股票**


如图 22.8 所示，Dendreon 公司（DNDN）因其前列腺癌药物的消息发布而出现急涨急跌。在以第2根K线为终点的两个月里，它暴涨 800%，并在随后的几个月里回吐了这波涨幅的 90%。接着它又暴涨 2,000%，涨到第7根K线，然后在接下来的三个月里下跌 50%。由于存在大涨大跌的风险，交易者只能做很小的量，而这么小的仓位规模，会抵消掉他们从那些大波动里本可以得到的收益。再加上这种不可预测性带来的压力，大多数交易者在身处这样的市场时，几乎不可能再去交易别的任何东西；而且他们很可能发现，避开这些特殊情况反而能赚更多的钱。看它们是有趣，但你的目标是赚大钱，不是在罕见的大行情之后、用很小的仓位赚到一点小钱，然后换来一阵情绪激动或毫无意义的权力感。


> As shown in Figure 22.8, Dendreon Corporation (DNDN) had sharp moves up and down due to news releases about its prostate cancer drug. It jumped 800 percent in the two months that ended at bar 2 and gave back 90 percent of that gain over the next couple of months. It then jumped 2,000 percent up to bar 7 and then fell 50 percent in the next three months. With the risk of huge moves up and down, traders can only trade small volume, and this reduced position size offsets any gain that they would get from the large swings. When you add the stress due to the unpredictability, it is almost impossible for most traders to trade anything else when they are in a market like this, and it is likely that they would make more money by avoiding these special situations. They are fun to watch, but your goal is to make a lot of money, not to get an emotional rush or a meaningless sense of power after making a little money from a small position after a rare big move.


# 第 23 章　期权

*23. Options*


期权我曾经和一位女交易者聊过，她经营着一家小企业，同时替自己和丈夫管理一个股票组合。有一天她醒来，发现组合比前一天跌了 500,000 美元。就在那一天，她成了一名日内交易者，决定再也不把交易留到隔夜。她看图很在行，但再也不愿意承担任何可能导致巨亏的隔夜敞口。其实另有一条路她本可以走：对于那些想持有几天到几周的交易，改用期权来做。她是个很强的交易者，本来完全可以继续用期权操作自己组合中相当大的一部分，不必把自己限制在日内交易上。我已经好几年没和她聊过了，但我相信，不管她是不是严格只做日内交易，她应该都做得不错；不过如果她把自己的策略里加上期权，也许还能做得更好。


> Options I once talked with a woman trader who was a small business owner and managed a stock portfolio for herself and her husband. One day, she awoke to find her portfolio was down $500,000 since the day before. On that day she became a day trader, deciding to never again carry trades home overnight. She was a good chart reader, but was no longer willing to have any overnight exposure that could result in a huge loss. As an alternative, she could have switched to option trading for trades that she wanted to hold for several days to several weeks. She was a strong trader and could have continued to trade a substantial part of her portfolio with options instead of restricting herself to day trading. I haven't talked with her in years, but I am confident that she is doing well whether or not she strictly day trades, but she might be doing better if she incorporated options into her strategies.


因为期权的买卖价差往往很宽，交易者通常只应考虑在更高时间级别的图表上做期权交易。任何交易者等式明显为正的建仓形态都是合理的。以下是交易者可以参照 60 分钟图或日线图考虑买入看涨期权或看跌期权的一些情形：


> Because the bid-ask spread is often wide for options, traders should usually only consider option trades on higher time frame charts. Any setup with a significantly positive trader's equation is reasonable. Here are some examples of situations when traders should can consider call or put purchases based on 60 minute or daily charts:


多头趋势中回调到移动平均线时买入看涨期权。空头趋势中上涨到移动平均线时买入看跌期权。在交易区间的底部买入看涨期权。在交易区间的顶部买入看跌期权。空头楼梯形态中，在出现新低时买入看涨期权。多头楼梯形态中，在出现新高时买入看跌期权。强劲多头突破中的一段多头急速行情里买入看涨期权。强劲空头突破中的一段空头急速行情里买入看跌期权。在交易区间底部、弱的低1或低2下方买入看涨期权。在交易区间顶部、弱的高1或高2上方买入看跌期权。


> Buying calls on a pullback to the moving average in a bull trend. Buying puts on a rally to the moving average in a bear trend. Buying calls at the bottom of a trading range. Buying puts at the top of a trading range. Buying calls at a new low in a bear stairs pattern. Buying puts at a new high in a bull stairs pattern. Buying calls during a bull spike in a strong bull breakout. Buying puts during a bear spike in a strong bear breakout. Buying calls below a weak low 1 or low 2 at the bottom of a trading range. Buying puts above a weak high 1 or high 2 at the top of a trading range.


你也可以依据更小的时间级别来做期权，比如 5分钟图：


> You can also trade options based on a smaller time frame like a 5 minute chart:


如果你是新交易者，账户资金有限，或者你想让自己的风险确定无疑，那么你可以买入 SPY 的看跌期权或看涨期权，而不是去交易 SPY 或 Emini 小型合约。对于 SPY 以及许多大盘股来说，近月平值（ATM）期权的买卖价差通常只有一个最小报价单位。这样一来，交易者就可以在 5分钟图上做交易，同时还能保有有利的交易者等式。在极少见的情况下，盘中价格波动大到你不愿意相信标的（比如 Emini 小型合约、股票、债券、外汇，或者你在交易的任何市场）的报价或成交，这时你可以用限价单买入看跌期权和看涨期权，做基于 5分钟图的日内交易。


> If you are a new trader and your account is limited or you want to be certain of your risk, you can buy SPY puts or calls instead of trading the SPY or Emini. The bid-ask spread is usually just one tick for the front month, at-the-money (ATM) options on the SPY, and many big cap stocks. This allows traders to place trades on the 5 minute chart and still have a favorable trader's equation. On rare occasions when the intraday price movement is so huge that you are unwilling to trust your quotes or your fills on the underlying (like the Emini, stocks, bonds, currencies, or whatever market you are trading), then you can buy puts and calls with limit orders for day trades based on 5 minute charts.


还有很多别的情形也值得做期权，还有很多其他有用的期权策略，但上面说的这些对日内交易者最容易操作，也最不分散注意力。如果交易者有能力应付其他类型的期权交易，那就该去做，但大多数活跃的日内交易者一旦做这些交易，就难免影响自己做日内交易赚钱的潜力。风险反转、零成本领口和比例价差总的来说都能提供出色的交易者等式，但很可能对日内交易者来说太分散注意力。这些单子下起来相对复杂，要下得正确需要高度专注。你要考虑的行权价和到期日很多；买卖价差往往很宽，于是这些交易让人感觉有点贵；而且你应当使用限价单，可它们往往不能很快成交。之后你还得管理这些交易，而且随着交易演变，常常还想做出调整。外汇交易者手里有股票组合时，若认为股市会下跌，会用外汇交易来做对冲：买入瑞郎、美元这类避险货币，同时做空瑞典克朗这类风险偏好货币，以取得同样的对冲效果。这样做省掉了期权的成本，但要求你熟悉外汇市场——那里的大量行情都发生在隔夜。所有这些对日内交易者来说都非常分散注意力，多数人要么选择专注做日内交易，要么只在自己交易里加入最简单的买入看跌期权或看涨期权。


> There are many other situations in which trading options is worthwhile, and there are many other useful option strategies, but the aforementioned are the easiest for a day trader and the least distracting. If traders are able to handle other types of option trading, they should trade them, but most active day traders cannot take those trades without interfering with their day trading earning potential. Risk reversals, cashless collars, and ratio spreads in general offer excellent trader's equations, but are probably too distracting for a day trader. The orders are relatively complicated to place and they require a lot of concentration to do them correctly. You have many strike prices and expirations to consider; the bid-ask spreads are often wide and therefore the trades feel a little expensive; and, you should use limit orders, but they often do not get filled quickly. You then have to manage the trades and often will want to make adjustments as the trades evolve. Forex traders will hedge their stock portfolios with currency trades, when they think that the stock market will fall, by buying risk-off currencies like the Swiss franc or the U.S. dollar and shorting risk-on currencies like the Swedish krona to get the same hedge. This avoids the cost of options, but requires a comfort with the foreign exchange (forex) market, where a lot of action takes place overnight. All of this is very distracting for a day trader, and most choose either to focus on day trading or to add only simple put or call purchases to their trading.


最省事的做法是：以买入看跌期权或看涨期权为主，有时买入价差组合，并打算把交易持有一到几天。你可以考虑允许市场朝你的持仓方向走出一个新的极值，也可以愿意加仓，因为用这些策略时你的风险是精确已知且有限的。在一个有可能形成的主要趋势反转顶部，你也可以单纯做空一小笔股票头寸，但你可能会忍不住在盘中盯它盯得太多，结果错过日内交易，最终把股票交易上的收益全部抵消掉。


> It is easiest to mostly buy puts or calls and sometimes spreads and look to hold the trades for one to several days. You can consider allowing one new extreme against your position, and you can be willing to add on because your risk is exactly known and limited with these strategies. At a possible major trend reversal top, you could also simply sell short a small stock position, but you might tend to watch it too much during the day, and this would cause you to miss day trades and ultimately negate any gains from the stock trade.


期权含有时间价值，它每天都在融化，让你的看跌期权或看涨期权贬值。如果你买入价差组合，两个行权价上的买价和卖价你都要吃亏，进场时亏一次，出场时再亏一次，而且手续费还是双份。因为有这些成本，交易者只能把自己限制在最好的那些期权建仓形态上。另外，只有在确实能提高自己的净收益时，才该把期权加进日内交易里，而对大多数交易者来说，情况并不会如此。对所有交易者来说，靠交易任何东西稳定赚钱都很难，而多数能赚钱的交易者通常选择专注做期权、期货或股票中的一样，而不是把注意力分给这三样。不过要清楚：期权交易者把股票头寸看作自己交易中不可分割的一部分，他们大多数人持有头寸是几天到几周，而不是像日内交易者那样几分钟到几小时。


> Options contain a time value that melts away every day, reducing the value of your put or call. If you buy a spread, you lose on the bid and on the ask on both strikes, both when you enter and when you exit the spread, and you have double the commissions. Because of these costs, traders have to restrict themselves to trading only the very best option setups. Also, they should add options to their day trading only if it truly results in an increase in their bottom line, which will not be the case for most traders. Trading anything profitably is difficult for all traders, and most profitable traders usually choose to focus on either options, futures, or stocks and not divide their attention among all three. However, be aware that options traders consider stock positions an integral component of their trading, and most hold their positions for days to weeks and not minutes to hours, like day traders.


还有另一种少见的情形，此时盘中做期权会比做期货和股票更可取。那就是市场正在暴跌、接近跌停的时候。如果出现了一个可靠的反转形态，你可能会觉得买入 Emini 小型合约的风险很小，哪怕仓位不大；但即便在信誉良好的经纪商那里，风险也可能很大。怎么会这样？因为系统可能过载，你的订单可能在 30 分钟甚至更久之后才被处理，或者才回报给你。如果你刚买进一个自以为是底部的价位，随后市场就跌穿了你的保护性止损，你电脑屏幕上可能仍然显示那张止损单在挂单中、尚未成交，尽管市场早已跌到它下方很多。那你怎么办？你不知道订单成交了没有，而等你打电话给经纪商询问时，又在电话上等了 30 分钟。大约 30 分钟之后，你的屏幕才会显示：那张本该已经成交的订单，带着一些滑点成交了。在这样一个巨大的空头日里，在经纪商的订单系统运转不正常的时候，你承受不起这么长时间的不确定性。


> There is one other rare occasion in which intraday options can be preferable to futures and stocks. That is when the market is in a huge free fall and it is close to limit down. If a reliable reversal pattern sets up, you might think that the risk of buying the Emini is small, even on a small position, but it can be substantial even with a reputable broker. How can that be? Because the system can get overloaded and your orders might not get processed or reported back to you for 30 minutes or more. If you just bought what you thought was a bottom and then the market fell through your protective stop, you might still see your stop order on your computer screen as a working, unfilled order, even though the market has fallen well below it. So what do you do? You don't know if the order got filled, and when you call your broker to find out, you are on hold for 30 minutes. Then after about 30 minutes, your computer screen will show that your order got filled with some slippage when it was supposed to have been filled. You cannot afford to live with this kind of uncertainty for such a long time on a huge bear day when your broker's order systems are not working correctly.


在 Emini 小型合约上，你很容易亏掉 10 点，因为经纪商从不为你的订单能否成交负责。一个替代办法是买入看涨期权，这样一旦你进场后市场开始暴跌，你的风险也是确定的。你可以试着用挂在看涨期权上的止损来限制潜在亏损，但即使市场远远跌穿你的止损、止损却没有成交，你至少知道自己的风险不是灾难性的，哪怕那张止损单从未被处理（前提是你的仓位规模合理）。市场怎么会跌穿你的保护性止损却不触发它？因为止损依据的是最后一笔成交，如果在你所持有的那个期权上根本没有成交，买价和卖价可能已经跌到你的止损下方很远，可你的止损就是不会成交，而你那张期权的价值会远低于你以为的水平。有一点很重要：期权里的保护性止损往往起不到任何保护作用；如果市场正快速朝你不利的方向走，你应该尽快用限价单出场。


> You could easily lose 10 points in the Emini since the broker is never responsible for your order getting filled. An alternative is to buy calls, so that you will be certain of your risk if the market goes into a free fall after you are in the market. You could try to limit any potential loss with a stop on your call, but even if the market falls far below your stop without it being filled, at least you know that your risk is not catastrophic even if the stop order was never processed (assuming that your position size was reasonable). How can the market fall through your protective stop and not trigger it? The stop is based on the last trade, and if no trades took place in your particular option, the bid and ask might fall too far below your stop, but your stop would not get filled and your option would be worth much less than you thought. It is important to understand that protective stops in options often offer no protection, and if the market is moving quickly against you, you should try to exit on a limit order as soon as you can.


你也可以考虑用 SPY 期权做日内交易，而不是做 SPY 或 Emini 小型合约，尤其是在你刚起步、又害怕巨亏的时候。举例来说，如果你买入一张一个月后到期的 SPY 平值（ATM）看涨期权，它可能花掉大约 250 美元，而且即便 SPY 跌到零，你最多也就亏这么多（显然，这里假定你买的是看涨期权，而且没有犯下那种错误——比如反过来裸卖看跌或看涨期权）。即使 SPY 在接下来一个小时里跌 1%，你大概也能在亏损不到 100 美元的情况下从这张看涨期权里出来。如果你是在多头趋势的一次回调中买入这张看涨期权，那么很可能可以带着 10 到 20 美分的盈利出场，换成钱就是 10 到 20 美元。这需要 SPY 走动大约 25 到 45 美分。如果 SPY 反而下跌 50 美分，你可能亏损大约 30 美分出场，也就是 30 美元。买入看跌或看涨期权，能让初学交易者更清楚自己最多承担多大风险，也许还能让他们更容易去思考该怎么交易，而不必时刻为钱数操心。


> You can also consider day trading SPY options instead of the SPY or the Emini, especially when you are starting out and if you are afraid of a huge loss. For example, if you buy a one-month-out, at-the-money (ATM) call in the SPY, it might cost about $250, which is the most that you could lose even if the SPY falls to zero (obviously this assumes that you bought the call and did not make a mistake, like instead shorting a naked put or call). Even if the SPY fell 1 percent over the next hour, you could probably get out of your call with under a $100 loss. If you bought the call during a pullback in a bull trend, the odds are good that you would be able to exit with a 10 to 20 cent profit, which translates into a $10 to $20 profit. This would require about a 25 to 45 cent move in the SPY. If the SPY instead fell 50 cents, you could get out of your call with maybe a 30 cent loss, which is $30. Buying puts or calls gives beginning traders more certainty about the most they have at risk, and this might make it easier for them to think about how to trade without constantly worrying about the dollars.


如果你在期货或股票市场一天只做几笔日内交易，那么就可以在期权市场里更活跃一些，尤其是如果你同时还在积极做股票波段交易。这类机会够再写一本书，不过这里有几句话值得说。举例来说，如果你做多一只在日线图上构筑底部的股票，并且愿意在更低的位置加仓，你可以在比市价低一档的行权价上卖出一张看跌期权。如果股票上涨、甚至只是小跌一点，你就把期权权利金收进口袋；如果股票反而跌破这张看跌期权的行权价，那么该期权的买方就会把股票行权给你（你会被迫按行权价买入股票），于是你就在那个更低的价位给自己手里的股票多头加了仓。


> If you take only a couple of day trades a day in the futures or stock markets, then you can be more active in the options market, especially if you also actively swing trade stocks. The opportunities could fill another book, but a few points are worth making here. For example, if you are long a stock that is basing on the daily chart and you are willing to add on lower, you could sell a put at one strike below the market. You collect the premium if your stock goes up or even drops a little, and if instead it goes down below the strike of the put, the buyer of that put will put the stock to you (you will be forced to buy it at the strike price) and you will therefore be adding to your long stock position at that lower price.


对持有股票多头的交易者来说，期权的另一种常见用法是卖出虚值（OTM）看涨期权，收取期权权利金。这种备兑看涨期权的卖出，每年可以为你的组合增加大约 10% 的收益，但它偶尔会把你从一只正在向上爆发的股票上赶出去。


> Another common use of options for traders who are long stock is to sell out-of-the-money (OTM) calls to collect premium. This covered call writing can add about a 10 percent return to your portfolio every year, but it will occasionally take you out of a stock that is exploding upward.


如果你预期某只股票或某个期货合约会出现大行情，却不知道方向，你可以买入跨式组合（同时买一张看跌期权和一张看涨期权），但这样你要同时承受两个腿上的时间价值衰减、手续费和买卖价差。跨式组合很少值得做。对期货交易者来说，另一个办法是把期货和期权组合成一个德尔塔中性头寸，也就是上涨和下跌的机会均等。举例来说，在 Emini 小型合约上，做多一手合约相当于买入 500 股 SPY 或 10 张平值看涨期权。如果你买入一手 Emini 合约（或 500 股 SPY）外加 10 张 ATM 看跌期权（或者反过来，做空一手 Emini 或 500 股 SPY，同时买入 10 张 ATM 看涨期权），那么在你下单的这一刻，这就是一个德尔塔中性头寸。市场一旦上涨或下跌，德尔塔就会变化。市场上涨时，你的 Emini 赚的会比看跌期权亏的多；市场下跌时，你的看跌期权赚的会比 Emini 亏的多。只有当市场横盘好几天时你才会亏钱，因为期权会随时间衰减。随着市场变化，你可以做很多微调来提高收益，但 Emini 日内交易者太忙了，没空把这套加进自己的交易。


> If you are expecting a big move in a stock or a futures contract but you don't know the direction, you can buy a straddle (buy both a put and a call), but then you suffer time decay, commissions, and bid-ask spreads on both legs. Straddles are rarely worthwhile. An alternative for futures traders is to combine the futures and options in a delta-neutral position, meaning that it has an equal chance of going up or down. For example, in the Emini, one long contract is equal to buying 500 SPY or 10 at-the-money calls. If you buy one Emini contract (or 500 SPY) and 10 ATM puts (alternatively, you could short one Emini or 500 SPY and buy 10 ATM calls), this is a delta-neutral position at the moment that you placed the trade. If the market moves up or down, the delta changes. If the market goes up, your Emini will make more than your puts will lose; if the market goes down, your puts will gain more than your Emini will lose. You lose money only if the market goes sideways for several days, because your option will decay. There is a lot of fine-tuning that you can do to increase your return as the market moves, but Emini day traders are too busy to add this to their trading.


期权交易者常谈到催化剂，也就是那些可能引发股票大行情的未来消息事件。最常见的是即将发布的财报，不那么常见的包括有关新产品的预期消息，或可能发生的收购。因为存在不确定性、又可能大涨或大跌，权利金通常会被大幅推高。消息一公布，权利金立刻被砸下去，砸得如此之狠，以至于你明明看到市场朝你预期的方向走出了大行情，却仍然亏钱！举例来说，假设你认为亚马逊（AMZN）的财报会很亮眼，于是在前一天以 5.00 美元买入一张看涨期权；财报确实亮眼，AMZN 开盘就涨了 5%；可是你这张看涨期权可能开盘只有 4.00 美元。你对财报和开盘方向的判断都没错，但权利金被推得那么高，AMZN 恐怕得涨上 10%，你这张看涨期权才会升值。由于这种被大幅推高的权利金会迅速流失，交易者在催化剂之前买入期权时必须小心。如果波动性太高，期权就很贵，需要一段巨大的行情才能赚钱。减轻这种影响的一个办法是买入价差组合，让你卖出的那张期权损失的权利金，大体抵消你买入那张期权的亏损；不过，价差组合通常只有在你打算持有一周或更久时才值得买，因为它们通常要出现大行情才会盈利，或者要出现一段较小的行情、同时到期日临近才会盈利。


> Option traders often talk about catalysts, which are upcoming news events that can lead to big moves in a stock. The most common one is an upcoming earnings report, and less common ones include anticipated information about new products or possible takeovers. Because there is uncertainty and the potential for a big move up or down is large, the premium is usually greatly inflated. As soon as the news is announced, the premium gets crushed, so much so that you can see the big move in the direction that you expected and still lose money! For example, suppose you thought that Amazon (AMZN)'s earnings were going to be strong so you bought a call for $5.00 on the day before, and the earnings were strong and AMZN went up 5 percent on the open; however, your call might open at only $4.00. You would be right about the strong earnings and the strong open, but the premium was so inflated that AMZN probably had to go up 10 percent for your call to increase in value. Because of this rapid loss of the greatly inflated premium, traders need to be careful when buying options before catalysts. If the volatility is too high, they are expensive and require a huge move to be profitable. One way to reduce the effect is to buy a spread so that your short option's loss of premium will largely offset the loss on your long option, but spreads are usually worth buying only if you plan to hold the position for a week or more, because they usually will be profitable only if there is a big move, or if there is a smaller move and expiration is approaching.


许多指数期权交易者会关注芝加哥期权交易所市场波动率指数（VIX），它往往与各大指数反方向运行，一般来说，当市场在恐慌中下跌、交易者大量买入看跌期权来对冲多头时，它会大幅上升。另一些交易者显然是在买看跌期权，赌空头趋势会延续。然而，市场开始重新转涨之后，看跌期权的买入量也可能增加，但原因不同。此时买看跌期权的，常常不是赌下跌的投机者，也不是害怕的多头在套保，而是信心十足的多头在保护自己新建立的多头仓位。如果是这种情况，这种看跌期权买入就意味着下行风险小得多。这些新多头愿意在抛售中继续持有股票头寸，因为他们买了看跌期权作保护；所以市场下跌时，他们会拿住自己的股票和期货头寸，而不是恐慌抛售、把市场进一步压下去。换句话说，这种看跌期权买入是一个信号：下行风险已经缩小，多头正变得有信心。不过，市场里整体的看跌期权买入究竟是在赌进一步下跌，还是在保护新多头，这根本无法分辨。靠电视上评论家的观点来建仓，永远不是一个好依据。要是他们真能靠交易赚大钱，大多数人就不会浪费时间在 CNBC 上高谈阔论了。


> Many index options traders pay attention to the Chicago Board Options Exchange Market Volatility Index (VIX), which tends to move in the opposite direction to the indexes and in general rises greatly when the market falls in a panic and traders are buying a huge number of puts to hedge their longs. Other traders are obviously buying puts as a bet that the bear trend will continue. However, after the market starts to turn up again, there can also be an increase in put buying, but for a different reason. Instead of speculators betting on a fall or scared longs hedging, it is often due to confident longs who are protecting their new longs. When this is the case, that put buying implies that the downside risk is much less. These new longs are willing to hold on to their stock positions during a sell-off because they bought the puts as protection, so if the market falls, they will hold on to their stock and futures positions instead of selling in a panic and driving the market down further. In other words, this put buying is a sign that the downside risk has shrunk and bulls are becoming confident. However, it is impossible to know whether the overall put purchases in the market are for speculation on further declines or for protection of new longs. Relying on the opinions of pundits on television is never a good basis for taking positions. If they could make a lot of money trading, most of them would not be wasting time pontificating on CNBC.


许多对冲基金买入股票，同时也买入看跌期权来对冲，标的要么是组合里的具体股票，要么是整个市场，比如 SPY 的看跌期权。对冲基金很少有完美对冲的，大多数会根据整体市场来调整看跌期权保护的数量。有些会用波动率指数来调整自己的看跌期权。举例来说，如果过去几周股市下跌 10%、导致波动率指数上升 20%，他们就会买回一部分或全部看跌期权，因为这些期权已经完成了它们的使命。他们当初是在市场更高的时候买入这些看跌期权的，用来防备股票组合遭遇抛售。如果市场真的抛售，他们的股票贬值，看跌期权就会升值。他们会在看跌期权上止盈，然后在等市场重新上涨期间，让自己处于对冲较少的状态；或者买入新的看跌期权，把对冲展期到更远月份的合约上，而且行权价通常更低。如果市场强劲上涨，而他们的对冲相对较少，他们就会买入更多看跌期权，以增加下行保护。


> Many hedge funds buy stock and hedge by also buying puts, either in the specific stocks in their portfolios or in the overall market, like SPY puts. Hedge funds are rarely perfectly hedged and most adjust the amount of put protection based on the overall market. Some use the volatility index to make adjustments in their puts. For example, if the volatility index rises 20 percent due to a 10 percent drop in the stock market over the past few weeks, they will buy back some or all of their puts, because the puts would have served their purpose. They initially bought the puts when the market was higher, as protection against a sell-off in their stock portfolio. If the market sells off and their stocks decrease in value, their puts will increase in value. They will take profits on their puts and either become less hedged while they wait for the market to rally again, or they will buy new puts to roll their hedge forward into a further out contract, and usually a lower strike price. If the market rallies strongly and they are relatively less hedged, they will buy more puts to increase their downside protection.


如果你在日线图或 60 分钟图上做期权，并且确信行情会在一两天内启动，那最好是直接买一张期权，而不是买价差组合。不过，如果你认为行情可能要一周或更久才会启动，那就可以通过买入价差组合来减轻时间价值衰减的影响。这样会降低你的总盈利，因为随着市场朝你有利的方向走，你卖出的那张期权价值会上升；但整体的风险回报比会变好。一般来说，卖出的那张期权的行权价要选在支撑或阻力区域附近。举例来说，如果 SPY 在 105，并且出现了强劲的买入信号，但 108 一带存在阻力，你可以买入一个月后到期的 ATM 105 看涨期权，并通过卖出行权价 108 的虚值看涨期权来抵掉一部分成本。买入这张看涨期权的成本，减去你卖出那张看涨期权收到的权利金，净成本也许是 1.20 美元左右。既然 108 是阻力位，而阻力位会像磁铁一样吸引价格，市场应该会被拉到 108 一带。两张看涨期权都会升值，但买入的 ATM 105 看涨期权升值更快，足以弥补卖出 108 看涨期权上的亏损还绰绰有余。如果市场以非常强劲的多头急速行情上涨，而你认为它能轻松突破 108 的阻力区，你可以亏损买回卖出的 108 看涨期权，继续持有买入的 105 看涨期权，后者的盈利足以抵消卖出那张期权的亏损还有余。如果向 108 的上涨走得很弱，而你认为市场可能会下跌，你就该带着盈利退出这个价差组合。通常不值得把价差组合持有到到期日，尽管那时的利润才是最大的。你的前提已经变了，所以你需要重新评估自己的头寸——做期权交易时，这一点永远要考虑。如果 SPY 在到期时处在 108，卖出的 108 看涨期权将一文不值地到期，买入的 105 看涨期权价值 3.00 美元，那么你的总净利润也许是 1.80 美元左右。但是，如果市场在 108、距离到期还有两周，而你的浮动净盈利是 1.50 美元，那也许干脆出场更好，因为为了把 1.50 美元的盈利熬成亏损——在到期前扛过一次跌到 105 以下的抛售——并不值得。随着市场涨到 108，你的风险回报状况已经改变，不再像你建仓时那么好。更好的做法是止盈，然后去找下一笔交易。


> If you are trading options on the daily or 60 minute charts and are confident that the move will begin within the next day or two, it is best to just buy an option instead of a spread. However, if you think that the move might take a week or more to begin, you can reduce the effect of time decay by purchasing a spread. You reduce your total profitability because the value of the short option increases as the market goes your way, but the overall risk/reward ratio improves. In general, choose the strike for the short option near a support or resistance area. For example, if the SPY is at 105 and has a strong buy signal, but there is resistance around 108, you could buy the one-month-out ATM 105 call and finance it in part by shorting the OTM 108 call. The net cost of the long call less the premium you collected on the short call might be about $1.20. Since 108 is resistance and resistance acts as a magnet, the market should get drawn to the 108 area. Both calls will increase in value, but the long ATM 105 call will increase in value faster and more than make up for the loss on the short 108 call. If the market rallies in a very strong bull spike and you think that it will easily break through the 108 resistance area, you can buy back the short 108 call for a loss and hold the long 105 call, which has more than enough profit to offset the loss on the short call. If the rally to 108 is weak and you think that the market might sell off, you should exit your spread with a profit. It is usually not worth holding the spread to expiration, even though that it when the maximum profit is realized. Your premise has changed so you need to reevaluate your position, and this is always a consideration when trading options. If the SPY is at 108 at expiration, the short 108 call will expire worthless and the long 105 call will be worth $3.00, so your total net profit might be about $1.80. However, if the market is at 108 with two weeks to go before expiration and your net open profit is $1.50, it is probably better to simply exit because it is not worth risking turning your $1.50 profit into a loss by sitting through a sell-off below 105 before expiration. As the market rallied to 108, your risk/reward situation changed, and it is no longer as good as it was when you put the trade on. It is better to take your profit and look for the next trade.


交易者既可以买入价差组合，也可以卖出价差组合。举例来说，如果 SPY 在 130，而某交易者认为它会涨，他可以买入一个看涨期权价差：买入 ATM 130 看涨期权，卖出一个行权价更高的虚值看涨期权，比如 133 看涨期权。他也可以用卖出一个看跌期权价差来做多押注，比如卖出 ATM 130 看跌期权、买入 OTM 125 看跌期权。一般来说，多数交易者更喜欢买入价差组合而不是卖出价差组合，因为他们更愿意做多而不是做空那个平值期权。如果他们做空了平值期权，而标的哪怕只朝他们不利的方向走一点点，他们就有可能揽上计划外的额外麻烦。举例来说，如果他们卖出了上面那个看跌期权价差，而 SPY 跌到 129 并在临近到期时一直停在那里，他们可能会被行权拿到股票，也就是经纪商会自动按 130 把股票卖给他们；接下来他们就得决定怎么处理这些股票，以及剩下那张买入的虚值看跌期权。


> A trader can either buy or sell a spread. For example, if the SPY is at 130 and a trader thinks that it will go up, he could buy a call spread by buying the ATM 130 call and selling an OTM call at a higher strike price, like a 133 call. He could also make a bullish bet by shorting a put spread, like selling an ATM 130 put and buying an OTM 125 put. In general, most traders prefer buying spreads to selling them because they prefer to be long and not short the ATM option. If they are short the ATM option and the underlying goes even a little against them, they are at risk of having additional, unwanted work. For example, if they shorted that put spread and the SPY fell to 129 and stayed there as expiration approached, they might be put the stock, which means that the broker will automatically sell them the stock at 130; then they would have to decide what to do with the stock and the remaining long OTM put.


买入价差组合通常最好是在你打算持有几周的时候，尤其是如果你能把这笔头寸持有到最后一个星期。原因是你卖出的那个行权价离平值总是更远；一个头寸越虚值，它因时间价值衰减而损失权利金的速度就越快，而这种衰减在最后一周会急剧加速。不过，如果你预期在那几天里会出现一段越过你卖出那个行权价的大行情，你也可以抱着只持有几天的打算去买一个价差组合。预期持有不到一周的交易，只有在你认为市场会在这周内越过你卖出的那个行权价时，才用价差组合。否则，就单纯买一张看涨期权或看跌期权。举例来说，假设 SPY 在 134，而你认为它会在接下来一周跌到 130。你要么可以买入一张看跌期权，比如 ATM 134 看跌期权；要么也许可以考虑一个价差组合，比如买入 134 看跌期权、卖出 132 或 131 看跌期权。


> Buying a spread is usually best when you plan to hold the trade for several weeks, especially if you can hold the position into the final week. This is because the short strike is always more OTM; the more a position is OTM, the faster it will lose premium through time decay, and that decay accelerates rapidly in the final week. However, you can also purchase a spread with the intention of holding it for just a few days if you are expecting a huge move beyond your short strike within that time. Buy the spread for a trade that you expect to hold for less than a week only if you think that the market will go beyond your short strike during that week. Otherwise, just buy a simple call or put. For example, say the SPY is at 134 and you think that it will fall to 130 over the next week. Either you could buy a put, like the ATM 134 put, or you might want to consider a spread, like a long 134 put and a short 132 or 131 put.


由于即使市场原地不动，期权每天也在亏钱，所以只有当你知道自己的前提依然成立时，才应该继续持有头寸。否则就出场，哪怕要亏。你怎么知道自己的前提还成不成立？看看此刻的市场，然后设想自己并没有持有这个头寸。接着问自己：你还会不会建立这样一笔一模一样的头寸？如果不会，那么你的前提就不成立了，应该立刻出场。


> Since options lose money every day even if the market remains unchanged, you should hold your position only if you believe that your premise is still valid. Otherwise, get out, even at a loss. How do you know if your premise is still valid? Look at the market as it is at this moment and imagine that you are not holding the position. Next, ask yourself if you would put on that exact position. If you would not, then your premise is invalid and you should exit immediately.


初学者常犯的一个错误，是把一笔已经盈利的期权头寸拿得太久。举例来说，如果交易者在交易区间底部买入一张看涨期权，打算在接下来一周里等价格上测到区间中部，可市场只用一天就冲到了目标位，那么这时候通常最好把大部分或全部利润先落袋。没错，这种强劲动能也许是多头趋势的开端，但更可能的情况是交易区间继续，接下来要么市场很快横盘，让权利金在时间价值衰减中被侵蚀掉，要么市场回调，利润就此消失。期权的利润消失得很快，所以一旦有了利润就把它收下，这一点非常重要。


> A common mistake that a beginner makes is to hold a winning option position too long. For example, if the trader buys a call at the bottom of a trading range with a goal of a test up to the middle of the range over the next week, but the market races to the target in just one day, it is usually better to take most or all of the profits at that point. Yes, the strong momentum might be the start of a bull trend, but it is more likely that the trading range will continue, and either the market will soon go sideways and erode the premium through time decay or the market will pull back and the profit will disappear. Option profits disappear quickly, so it is very important to take them once you have them.


不要因为一只股票名气大，就以为它的期权成交很活跃。如果不活跃，买卖价差可能大得让人吃不消。举例来说，一张 ATM 看涨期权的买价也许是 1.20 美元，卖价也许是 1.80 美元。这意味着你大概得付 1.80 美元才能买下这张看涨期权，而如果你立刻卖掉，只能收到 1.20 美元，瞬间亏掉 60 美分，也就是你投入的三分之一！一般来说，如果你考虑的那个行权价上，未平仓合约量低于 1,000，或者近期日成交量低于 300 张期权，你通常就不该下这笔单。成交稀少的期权，你几乎永远不该去交易。不过，如果你真去做了，就一定要用限价单进场和出场。即便如此，你的限价单也可能挂在那里几个小时，而你一直在等它成交，有时最后你会让步、按市价出场，盈利的潜力因此大打折扣。像 SPY 这样活跃的期权市场，好处之一就是近月合约里 ATM 和接近平值的期权，买卖价差通常只有一个美分，所以你可以下市价单，还能拿到极好的成交价。


> Just because a stock is well-known, do not assume that its options are heavily traded. If they are not, the bid-ask spread can be unacceptably large. For example, the bid for an ATM call might be $1.20 and the ask might be $1.80. This means that you would probably have to pay $1.80 for the call, and if you immediately sold it you would receive $1.20, instantly losing 60 cents, or a third of your investment! In general, if the open interest is less than 1,000 or the recent daily volume is less than 300 options for the strike that you are considering, you usually should not place the trade. You should rarely, if ever, trade thinly traded options. However, if you do, you should always enter and exit with limit orders. Even then, your limit order might sit there for hours while you are waiting for it to get filled, and you will sometimes end up giving in and exiting at the market, greatly reducing your profit potential. One of the nice things about active option markets like the SPY is that the bid-ask spread for the front month is usually only a penny for ATM and near-the-money options, so you can place market orders and get excellent fills.


单凭买卖价差大，并不该成为阻止你买期权的理由，因为价差与股票价格是成比例的。当 AAPL 在 300 美元交易时，一张 ATM 看涨期权的买卖价差也许是 20 美分，这在初学者眼里可能显得很多。可是，一只在 30 美元交易的股票，只要它的期权买卖价差是 2 美分，交易者买起来不会有半点犹豫。他们可能每买一张 AAPL 看涨期权，就会买 10 张那只 30 美元股票的看涨期权。从数学上讲，这才是合适的交易方式。


> A large bid-ask spread alone should not be a deterrent to buying an option, because the spread is proportional to the price of the stock. When AAPL is trading at $300, the bid-ask spread on an ATM call might be 20 cents, which might seem like a lot to a beginner. However, traders would not hesitate to buy an option on a stock trading at $30 if the bid-ask spread on the option was 2 cents. They might buy 10 calls of the $30 stock for every one AAPL call. This is a mathematically appropriate way to trade.


如果你是在日线图上一段强劲急速行情中进场，而市场距离目标还有一段路要走，价差组合可能很有用。举例来说，如果 SPY 在 118，正处于一段新的空头趋势中、并在均线下方很远处快速下跌，而你认为它会在接下来几天里触及 115，那么你可能不太敢买看跌期权，因为市场有可能在跌到目标之前突然反转向上、回到均线。作为替代，你可以买入 118 看跌期权、卖出 115 看跌期权。如果市场在接下来两天里不停地下跌到 115 支撑区，你的看跌期权价差组合也许能以 1.50 美元的盈利出场。如果它反而上涨到均线处的 120，你的价差组合可能出现一美元的浮动亏损。如果你相信自己的前提依然完好，你可以分批拆解这个价差组合：把卖出的那张看跌期权买回来，赚个 50 美分左右，同时继续持有买入的那张看跌期权。如果你判断正确，市场在接下来一周里跌到 115 的目标位，你也许能在买入的那张看跌期权上再赚 2.00 美元，整笔交易总盈利大约 2.50 美元。在市场对你不利时能拆解价差组合，需要经验；但如果你对自己的看图能力有信心，这不失为一个好办法。


> Spreads can be useful if you are entering during a strong spike on the daily chart and the market has a way to go before it reaches its target. For example, if the SPY is at 118 and falling sharply well below the moving average in a new bear trend, and you believe that it will hit 115 within the next few days, you might be hesitant to buy a put, because the market might suddenly reverse up to the moving average before falling to the target. As an alternative, you can buy a 118 put and short a 115 put. If the market falls nonstop over the next couple of days to the 115 support area, you could exit your put spread for maybe a $1.50 profit. If instead it rallied to 120 at the moving average, your spread might have an open loss of a dollar. If you believed that your premise was still intact, you could leg out of your spread by buying back your short put for a profit of maybe 50 cents, but holding your long put. If you are right and the market then falls to your 115 target over the next week, you might make an additional $2.00 on the long put for a total profit of about $2.50 on the trade. It takes experience to be able to leg out of a spread when the market is going against you, but if you are confident about your chart reading, this can be a good approach.


顺便说一句，在支撑位和阻力位上卖出的期权会增强这些价位的强度，因为期权往往会在未平仓合约量最大的那个行权价附近到期。任何一个期权行权价上的成交量越大，那个价位的磁力效应就越强，该价位上的支撑和阻力也就越强。如果成交量足够大，它甚至能影响到期日附近的市场。如果存在一个明显的支撑或阻力位，成交量可能变得极其巨大，因为那个行权价会引发大量期权交易。事实上，SPY 和 QQQ 常常就在未平仓合约量最大的看跌期权和看涨期权行权价附近到期。期权的卖方通常是机构，也就是聪明钱交易者；他们会在期权市场和相关的市场里想尽办法，让自己卖出的期权一文不值地到期，从而把他们收到的权利金全部留下。


> Incidentally, short options at support and resistance levels increase the strength of those levels, since options tend to expire near the strike price with the biggest open interest. The more volume traded at any option strike price increases the magnetic effect of that price, which increases the support and resistance at that price. If the volume is large enough, it can affect the market around expiration. The volume can get huge if there is an obvious support or resistance level, because that strike price will generate lots of option activity. In fact, the SPY and the QQQ often expire close to the put and call strike price with the largest open interest. The short side of the options is usually taken by institutions, who are the smart money traders, and they will do whatever they can in the options market and in related markets to make their short options expire worthless so they get to keep the entire premium that they collected.


VIX 衡量的是标普 500 指数期权的波动性。在一段强劲的多头急速行情里，当你认为后续行情很可能出现时，买入看涨期权、或者买入 SPY 或 Emini 小型合约通常是不错的交易，但这里有一个与 VIX 相关的风险。顺便说一句，VIX 每 16 点对应标普 500 指数预期日均区间 1%（所以 VIX 为 32 意味着 SPY 和 Emini 的日均区间大约是 2%）。如果急速行情足够强，VIX 也可能急速上升，你买入看涨期权时成本就会偏高。如果接下来几个小时的行情进入一段平静的多头通道，VIX 可能跌得足够多，以至于你的看涨期权不会升值。因此，如果你想在多头急速行情里买看涨期权，或在空头急速行情里买看跌期权，而你不是在急速行情的早期买入，那就最好等一次回调，以降低在 VIX 短暂急升时买入的风险——那种急升会让所有期权短暂地定价过高。


> The VIX is a measure of the volatility of the S&P 500 index options, and although buying a call or the SPY or the Emini is usually a good trade during a strong bull spike when you believe that follow-through is likely, there is a risk associated with the VIX. Incidentally, every 16 points in the VIX corresponds to a 1 percent expected average daily range in the S&P 500 index (so a VIX of 32 means that the average daily range of the SPY and Emini is about 2 percent). If the spike is strong enough, the VIX might also spike up and the cost of your call would be elevated at the time of your purchase. If over the next couple of hours the market enters a quiet bull channel, the VIX might fall enough so that the value of your call will not increase. Because of this, if you want to buy a call during a bull spike or a put during a bear spike, if you are not buying early on in the spike, it is better to wait for a pullback to reduce the risk of buying during a brief spike up in the VIX, which would cause a brief overpricing of all options.


期权波动性的急剧上升，通常会导致虚值期权的价格出现不成比例的上涨。这叫作偏斜；偏斜的定价会让初学价差交易的交易者感到不快，因为它带来的利润比看起来公允或合乎逻辑的水平要小。假设某交易者在多头市场的交易区间中，于 SPY 处在 133 附近时买入一个 133/128 看跌期权价差：为 133 看跌期权付出 3.50 美元，为卖出 128 看跌期权收到 2.00 美元；随后市场因某场世界性危机在两周内下跌 4.00 美元，这位交易者可能会以为价差组合也会上涨 4.00 美元。然而，正因为市场快速下跌时，有那么多交易者在买入虚值看跌期权来保护自己的多头，它们的价格相对平值看跌期权涨得不成比例，这个价差组合可能只涨到 2.50 美元左右，也就是赚 1.00 美元。市场急剧下跌时波动性急剧上升，而波动性对虚值看跌期权（以及看涨期权）的影响更大。不过，在到期前的几周里，市场可能得跌破较低那个行权价大约 5%、也许一路跌到 123，这个价差组合才能有接近 5.00 美元的利润。只有市场远远跌破较低那个行权价，或者在到期前最后一周，价差组合才能接近它的盈利潜力。一般来说，交易者只有在预期接下来几周内市场会走到接近自己卖出那一腿的位置时，或者愿意持有价差组合、在到期前后一周左右出场时，才该买入价差组合。如果到期时 SPY 低于较低的行权价 128，这个看跌期权价差组合在到期时就能拿到完整的 5.00 美元利润，但多数交易者在到期之前就已经出场了。


> A dramatic increase in option volatility usually causes a disproportionate increase in price of the OTM options. This is called skew, and skewed pricing can be upsetting to beginning spread traders, because it results in smaller profits than what seems fair or logical. If a trader bought a 133/128 put spread in the SPY during a trading range in a bull market when the SPY was around 133, paying $3.50 for the 133 put and receiving $2.00 for the short 128 put, and the SPY fell $4.00 over the next two weeks on some world crisis, the trader might assume that the spread would increase by $4.00 as well. However, since so many traders are buying OTM puts to protect their longs as the market is falling sharply, their price increases disproportionately to the ATM puts, and the spread might increase to only about $2.50, or a $1.00 profit. As the market falls sharply, the volatility increases sharply, which has a greater effect on OTM puts (and calls, as well). However, the market might have to fall about 5 percent below the lower strike price, maybe down to 123, for the spread to have close to a $5.00 profit in the weeks before expiration. Spreads get close to their profit potential only if the market falls far below the lower strike price, or during the last week before expiration. Traders should generally buy spreads only if they are expecting a move to near their short leg at some point over the next few weeks, or if they are willing to hold the spread and exit within a week or so of expiration. The put spread will have the full $5.00 profit at expiration if the SPY is less than 128, the lower strike price, at expiration, but most traders exit before then.


由于日线图上出现大幅急速行情时虚值期权会发生偏斜，如果交易者预期接下来一周左右市场会向上或向下走出一段行情，就应该考虑直接买入期权。如果他们打算在到期前好几周就出场，就应该考虑不要买价差组合。举例来说，如果市场刚刚在日线图上强劲下跌 3%，现在回调到了一个可能是更低的高点的位置，而交易者预期接下来几天会开始一段强劲的第二波下跌，那么他们也许干脆直接买入看跌期权，而不是买价差组合。如果他们本来愿意花总共 3.00 美元买两个看跌期权价差，那么不妨改为考虑花大约 3.50 美元买一张 ATM 看跌期权。如果接下来一周左右真的出现了他们预期的急跌，而市场迅速跌到 128，这张看跌期权也许值 7.50 美元。这仍然少于他们可能希望赚到的 5.00 美元（也就是他们买入看跌期权时 SPY 的 133 与当前 128 之间的差价），但远多于两个看跌期权价差能赚到的 2.00 美元。如果几天之内这张看跌期权就迅速升值 3.00 或 4.00 美元，他们就应该平掉这个头寸，因为市场很可能会回调、进入一段交易区间。如果他们继续持有这张看跌期权，4.00 美元的利润可能很快变成 2.00 美元。那段上涨也许还会让他们相信自己的前提已经不再成立，于是带着那 2.00 美元的利润出场，心里后悔自己太贪。期权市场常常送交易者一些意外的礼物，但很少像初学者以为的那么合乎逻辑。当礼物真的来了，几乎总是先收下它，然后再去找下一笔交易。


> Because of the skewing of OTM options during big spikes on the daily chart, traders should consider outright option purchases if they are expecting a move up or down over the next week or so. If they are planning to exit several weeks before expiration, they should consider not buying a spread. For example, if the market just had a strong 3 percent drop on the daily chart and now has pulled back to a possible lower high, and traders expect a strong second leg down to begin within the next few days, they are probably better off just buying an outright put instead of a spread.
